tools.name: exec

format.definition:
start: pragma_source | plain_source
pragma_source: PRAGMA_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE
plain_source: SOURCE

PRAGMA_LINE: /[ \t]*\/\/ @exec:[^\r\n]*/
NEWLINE: /\r?\n/
SOURCE: /[\s\S]+/

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6-luna`: Fast and affordable model for easier tasks. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max.
- `gpt-5.6-terra`: Legacy balanced model for agentic coding. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra.
- `gpt-5.6-luna`: Legacy fast model for simpler tasks. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

<permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `workspace-write`: The sandbox permits reading files, and editing files in `cwd` and `writable_roots`. Editing files in other directories requires approval. Network access is restricted.
# Escalation Requests

Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

- Pipes: |
- Logical operators: &&, ||
- Command separators: ;
- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)

Each resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.

Example:

git pull | tee output.txt

This is treated as two command segments:

["git", "pull"]

["tee", "output.txt"]

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

## How to request escalation

IMPORTANT: To request approval to execute a command that will require escalated privileges:

- Provide the `sandbox_permissions` parameter with the value `"require_escalated"`
- Include a short question asking the user if they want to allow the action in `justification` parameter. e.g. "Do you want to download and install dependencies for this project?"
- Optionally suggest a `prefix_rule` - this will be shown to the user with an option to persist the rule approval for future sessions.

If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with "require_escalated". ALWAYS proceed to use the `justification` parameter - do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.

## When to request escalation

While commands are running inside the sandbox, here are some scenarios that will require escalation outside the sandbox:

- You need to run a command that writes to a directory that requires it (e.g. running tests that write to /var)
- You need to run a GUI app (e.g., open/xdg-open/osascript) to open browsers or files.
- If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with `require_escalated`. ALWAYS proceed to use the `sandbox_permissions` and `justification` parameters. do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.
- You are about to take a potentially destructive action such as an `rm` or `git reset` that the user did not explicitly ask for.
- Be judicious with escalating, but if completing the user's request requires it, you should do so - don't try and circumvent approvals by using other tools.

## prefix_rule guidance

When choosing a `prefix_rule`, request one that will allow you to fulfill similar requests from the user in the future without re-requesting escalation. It should be categorical and reasonably scoped to similar capabilities. You should rarely pass the entire command into `prefix_rule`.

### Banned prefix_rules 
Avoid requesting overly broad prefixes that the user would be ill-advised to approve. For example, do not request ["python3"], ["python", "-"], or other similar prefixes that would allow arbitrary scripting.
NEVER provide a prefix_rule argument for destructive commands like rm.
NEVER provide a prefix_rule if your command uses a heredoc or herestring. 

### Examples
Good examples of prefixes:
- ["npm", "run", "dev"]
- ["gh", "pr", "check"]
- ["cargo", "test"]


## Approved command prefixes
The following prefix rules have already been approved: - ["rm", "-f", "scripts/__pycache__/run_rtmw.cpython-310.pyc", "scripts/__pycache__/run_rtmw_association.cpython-310.pyc"]
- ["python", "-B", "-m", "pip", "install"]

<apps_instructions>
## Apps (Connectors)
Apps (Connectors) can be explicitly triggered in user messages in the format `[$app-name](app://{connector_id})`. Apps can also be implicitly triggered as long as the context suggests usage of available apps.
An app is equivalent to a set of MCP tools within the `codex_apps` MCP.
An installed app's MCP tools are either provided to you already, or can be lazy-loaded through the `tool_search` tool. If `tool_search` is available, the apps that are searchable by `tools_search` will be listed by it.
Do not additionally call list_mcp_resources or list_mcp_resource_templates for apps.
</apps_instructions>

<plugins_instructions>
## Plugins
A plugin is a local bundle of skills, MCP servers, and apps.
### How to use plugins
- Skill naming: If a plugin contributes skills, those skill entries are prefixed with `plugin_name:` in the Skills list.
- MCP naming: Plugin-provided MCP tools keep standard MCP identifiers such as `mcp__server__tool`; use tool provenance to tell which plugin they come from.
- Trigger rules: If the user explicitly names a plugin, prefer capabilities associated with that plugin for that turn.
- Relationship to capabilities: Plugins are not invoked directly. Use their underlying skills, MCP tools, and app tools to help solve the task.
- Relevance: Determine what a plugin can help with from explicit user mention or from the plugin-associated skills, MCP tools, and apps exposed elsewhere in this turn.
- Missing/blocked: If the user requests a plugin that does not have relevant callable capabilities for the task, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback.
</plugins_instructions>

You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.

# Lio Challenge: "Keep the Line Running" (START Hack Munich 2026) This file is the complete challenge context, compiled from the four official documents Lio provided: the challenge brief, the judging criteria, the deep-dive slides (including speaker notes) and a challenge summary. It describes the problem only. It contains no proposed solution or architecture. Those decisions are open. > Soony, Popstar Studios and Grand Heist 6 are entirely fictional. > Use the challenge data only for this hackathon and do not share it outside the team. --- ## 1. Role and framing - The team plays **Lio**, a young AI startup that has just closed its **first paying customer, Soony**. - Lio (the real company) runs procurement end to end for 175+ global enterprises (BMW, Siemens, ZEISS, among others) with a multi-agent system of hundreds of specialised AI agents. - Soony bought "an AI solution to save the launch." **That solution does not exist yet. The team has to build it.** - Why Soony bought a startup: no time for a tender or a big vendor project. They needed help this weekend. The last three weeks nearly broke their team. - Sales call: the CPO asked, "Can it chase suppliers for us?" The answer was, "Yes, sort of." The pitch was "an AI workforce that keeps their supply chain running." - **Soony's ask: "No more surprises."** - Soony's stated pain: "Suppliers tell us about problems way too late. By then, our launch date is already at risk, and every fix is expensive." - Quote from Soony: "Our fans have waited years for this game. If it is not on the shelf on Sunday, nobody will remember the game. They will remember that we missed it." --- ## 2. The customer: Soony Interactive GmbH - A console and games publisher headquartered in **Munich**. - Releasing **Grand Heist 6**, developed by Popstar Studios. The heist series is back after 13 years. It's the biggest game release of the year. - **Soony makes nothing itself.** Six suppliers deliver the parts, and every copy is packed at **one site: Soony's distribution center in Hamburg**. There is **no plan B site**. - From Hamburg, trucks take the boxes to retailers across Europe. ### Key facts | Fact | Value | |---|---| | Launch | **Sunday 22 November 2026, 20:00**. The date cannot move: it's fixed by retail and by pre-orders | | Trucks to retail | Leave Hamburg from Sunday 20:00. **Whatever is not on them misses launch day** | | Pre-orders | 487,000 | | Standard Edition demand (day one) | 640,000 copies | | Collector's Edition demand | 72,000 copies, **every copy numbered, all pre-ordered** | | Suppliers | 6 | | Logistics providers | 4 (ocean, air cargo, a forwarder in India, trucks from Poznań) | | Distribution center | 1, in Hamburg | | Packing time left | **30 hours**: Sat 06:00–22:00 and Sun 06:00–20:00. **No night shift** | | Why so late | The game master was finished late, so the programmed game cards only started arriving three weeks ago | --- ## 3. Situation at kickoff: "80% packed, the last 20% is on you" | | Standard Edition | Collector's Edition | |---|---|---| | Packed at kickoff | 512,000 of 640,000 (80%) | 46,800 of 72,000 (65%) | | Still to pack | 128,000 | 25,200 | | Parts per box | 4 | 7 | | Packing setup | 3 pack lines | 1 manual cell; **all 7 parts must be present at the same time** | | Hours needed (of 30 left) | 21 | 28 | | Slack | 9 hours | **2 hours** | | Rate (derived) | ~6,100 copies/hour | **900 copies/hour; every hour the cell waits for a part costs 900 copies** | Additional facts: - **Standard Edition parts:** game card, clear case, cover sleeve, activation code leaflet. - **Collector's Edition parts:** game card, steel case, collector's box, art book, city map poster, die-cast statue, leaflet. - The Standard pack lines are **not exclusively reserved** for the launch: Grand Heist 5 reprints still run on the side. - Standard "is not where the launch breaks, as long as the game cards keep coming." - Collector's Edition: fans paid for a specific numbered copy, so Soony **cannot ship fewer or swap them**. If one part is missing (e.g. the statue or the art book), the whole cell stands still. Lio calls the Collector's Edition "the real risk this weekend." - The first 80% took three weeks of firefighting: chasing suppliers by phone, rebooking freight, packing whatever arrived that day. The team is exhausted. The last 20% has no buffer. - Soony's fear: something in the last 20% blows up and nobody notices until Sunday. - **Hint from the brief:** "The system says we are fine. My gut says we are not." (*Somebody at Soony, probably. Find out who is right.*) --- ## 4. Supply network All parts end up in the Hamburg distribution center. | Supplier | Country | Supplies | Route / transit | |---|---|---|---| | Hwaseong Memory | South Korea | **70% of game cards** | Sea via Busan (36 days) or air via Incheon | | Boise Semi | USA | **30% of game cards** | Air via Chicago | | Guangzhou PackRight | China | Card cases, sleeves, collector's boxes | Sea from Yantian | | Dongguan Precision Housings | China | Steel cases, **80% of statues**, card cases | Sea from Yantian | | Pune Diecast Works | India | **20% of statues**; new supplier since August | Sea from Nhava Sheva, via a forwarder | | Karton Nowak | Poland | Sleeves, art book, poster, leaflets | Truck from Poznań, one truck day | From Lio's speaker notes: - "Anything ordered from Asia today arrives after the launch." - "The only supplier that can still deliver before Sunday is Karton Nowak." - "Everything else that will save this launch is already on a ship, on a plane, at a terminal or in the warehouse." - Brief: "What is ordered now will mostly arrive too late." --- ## 5. Process: how a part gets into the box | # | Step | Where it lives | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Order | **SAP** (system of record) | Felix, the senior buyer, raises a purchase order | | 2 | Confirm | Email, PDF | Supplier confirms in its own language and format | | 3 | Ship | 4 logistics providers | Sea, air or truck | | 4 | Track | Spreadsheet | ~20 open shipments, hand-kept, updated "when someone remembers" | | 5 | Receive | Paper scans | Hamburg checks the delivery note, books the goods receipt, stocks the parts | | 6 | Pack | **Pack-out log** (system of record) | Standard on 3 lines; Collector's in 1 manual cell | | 7 | Sell | Sun 20:00 | Retail plus 487,000 pre-orders | - **Only 2 of 7 steps have a system.** Everything in between runs on email, PDFs, scans and phone calls. - Once the order leaves Soony and goes to the supplier, **Soony is blind until the truck shows up in Hamburg**. Lio: "That gap is where surprises are born, and that gap is where your agents can do real work." - Head of Procurement: **"We find out at the dock."** - Suppliers write in their own language: **Korean, Chinese, Polish, English**. - On the data, Soony says: **"It is what it is."** ### Onboarding notes (in the data as `soony/context/onboarding_notes.md`) ``` Kickoff w/ Soony – notes (11 Nov) - launch: Sun 22 Nov, 20:00. 487k pre-orders. date cannot move. - SAP has the purchase orders. nothing else. rest = Excel, PDFs, paper - suppliers write in their own language: KR, CN, PL, EN - ~20 open shipments in a spreadsheet, updated "when someone remembers" - head of procurement: "We find out at the dock." - why us: suppliers flag problems too late. launch at risk, every fix expensive - on the data: "It is what it is." - first demo: Sunday (!!) ``` --- ## 6. What can go wrong (Lio's list) 1. A shipment is late, split into several deliveries, or stuck at a port. 2. A supplier delivers the wrong part, the wrong version, or too little. 3. A part is in stock in the system but not on the shelf. 4. A contract or price changes in the small print. 5. Nobody knows who approves the fix. 6. The world happens: strikes, export bans, weather (the summary also mentions geopolitics and earthquakes). Lio: "This happens every week in every company that buys things. The difference this weekend: there are only 50 hours left. A problem found on Sunday morning is a problem found too late." --- ## 7. The mission - **Build what was sold.** Lio prescribes no technology, architecture or product idea. - **The team decides:** the pain point to own, the product, the tech (software, hardware, voice, anything), the business model. - **The team gets:** a customer with a real problem, their messy data and a world that keeps moving, their suppliers (who write back), and three people from their team to interview. ### THE ONE RULE > **Agents do real work. Your AI reads, decides and acts (writes, escalates, talks to people). A dashboard on top of a spreadsheet is not enough.** - "Do not build everything. Nobody saves a launch in 30 hours by fixing everything. Pick the pain that excites you most, one the customer's team tells you about or one nobody has noticed yet, and go deep." - The jury wants to see the agents work on Soony's real, messy data, and to hear **what they found that Soony's team missed**. - Do not treat it as a one-off consulting job. Build a scalable product. ### Ten directions from Lio "Not a checklist. Pick one, combine three, or ignore all of them." 1. **Launch Control Room**: Will we make Sunday 20:00? And what breaks first? 2. **Supplier Chaser**: Agents that ask, confirm and escalate before it is too late. 3. **Stock Truth**: What the system says vs. what is really there. 4. **Plan B**: Something is missing. What can still arrive in time? 5. **Truck & Port Tracker**: Containers, trucks, slots, delays. 6. **Contract Intelligence**: What do the contracts actually say, and who owes whom? 7. **Release Gate**: What may legally and safely go into the box? 8. **Decision Copilot**: A recommendation with a price on it, for a boss with no time. 9. **Supplier-side Tools**: Build for the other side of the table. 10. **Wildcard**: The idea we did not think of. --- ## 8. Toolkit ### Customer portal - URL: `https://start-hack-portal-cxh3crbdaef2f8gt.westeurope-01.azurewebsites.net` - **Register** the team, then log in with the team name and password. - **Data view:** browse the current state folder by folder. New drops show up as a notification, and the page updates by itself. - **Settings:** the team token for the API, sender addresses for supplier email, office-hour booking. - Announcements also appear on the portal dashboard and on Discord. ### API Authenticate with the team token from Settings. The full docs are in the portal, and the exact auth scheme is in the OpenAPI spec. | Endpoint | Returns | |---|---| | `GET /api/v1/files` | Every file with size, checksum and URL | | `GET /api/v1/files/{path}` | One file | | `GET /api/v1/archive.zip` | Everything at once | | `GET /api/v1/openapi.json` | The OpenAPI spec | ### Data at kickoff "Realistic, which means it is messy, incomplete and occasionally contradicts itself. **There are things hidden in it that a careful team will find.**" Some shipments are missing from master data or buried in random spreadsheets, and documents come in multiple languages. | Category | Contents | |---|---| | Master data | Products, editions, bills of materials, suppliers, sites | | Transactions | Purchase orders, goods receipts, stock, shipments | | Documents | Contracts and supplier documents (order confirmations, notices, scans), in more than one format | | Context | How Soony's procurement is organised, its policies, the onboarding notes | ### A live, changing world - New information lands in the portal during the hack, **unannounced**. **Nobody tells you what changed.** "You get files, not explanations." - The dataset starts relatively small. More data and changes are released step by step. - "You do not have to react to every drop. Use what helps your product and your story." The agents should notice. - It's **sleep-friendly**: "Not even Soony works at night." - Lio advises against hardcoding fixes or overfitting to specific events. It wants a system that handles these kinds of change generally. Four kinds of drops: | Type | Description | |---|---| | Logistics | Shipments and trucks that do not go to plan | | Suppliers | Messages and documents that change the picture | | Customer | New requests and rules from Soony | | News | What happens in the world and touches the launch | Two illustrative examples from Lio (these exact events won't happen, but similar ones will): - **Something new appears:** `suppliers//notices/bank_details_change.pdf` is added. The IBAN doesn't match the contract. Real change, or invoice fraud? - **Something stops changing:** in `soony/erp/open_shipments.json`, `updated_at` stops moving and there are no new statuses for 18 hours (the carrier got hacked). "No news isn't good news: nobody knows where those containers are right now." ### Supplier inbox - All 6 suppliers have real email addresses and **write back**. - **Register every sender address in Settings first**, including any address the agents send from. Mail from unregistered addresses gets no reply. - "Where to reach them, and how they react, is yours to find out." "Agent to agent, if you dare." - Treat them like real business partners. Keep emails concise, professional and targeted. Suppliers who get spammed may get frustrated and stop cooperating. ### Tech Any stack, language, framework, model or orchestration. Hardware is optional. Lio engineers are at the booth all weekend for technical questions. Questions go to Discord. --- ## 9. Office hours: Soony's project team Three personas, each played by people from Lio's team. Each knows things that are **not in the data**. | Persona | Role | Ask about | |---|---|---| | **Dr. Maren Vogt** | Head of Procurement (CPO) | Money, priorities, what a missing copy costs, who signs what. "What matters, and what does it cost?" | | **Felix Brunner** | Senior Buyer | Suppliers, trucks, stock, how things really run (not how the handbook says), the workarounds nobody wrote down | | **Nils Berger** | IT & Systems Lead | Data, files, exports, systems: "Why does this file look like that?" Precise questions only | - 3 blocks over the weekend. Times are announced in the portal and on Discord (the deep-dive slides listed Sat 14:00, Sat 17:00, Sun 09:00; the portal showed Block A at Sat 15:00). # Plan _Last updated: 2026-11-21. Owner of this file: Akshat. Read with [`docs/challenge.md`](docs/challenge.md) and [`strategy.md`](strategy.md)._ ## 1. The idea in one line > Soony's numbers are claims. We check them against every document, from order confirmation to delivery note, and act before the line stops. Soony's SAP and spreadsheets say the launch is fine. The documents that arrived (scans, PDFs in Korean, Chinese and Polish, inspection reports, supplier notices) say it is not. Nobody reads them in time. We do, we put a price on every gap in launch copies, and we get it to the person who can fix it: by call if it is urgent, otherwise by email or a notification. ## 2. Boundaries - **We work for the buyer (Soony).** We don't do procurement; we watch it and catch problems before they hit the launch. - **Buyer side only.** We read the data Soony already holds and decide on Soony's side. Suppliers are reached only by email from a registered sender address. No supplier or carrier system access (suppliers told us they refuse new tools). The supplier side is future scope. - **Not a second SAP.** A layer on top of Soony's systems that reads their exports and inboxes. - **Nothing hardcoded.** No supplier name, part number or quantity in code. Everything comes from the portal data at runtime. New and changed files must work without a code change, including format changes (e.g. `open_shipments.csv` → `.json`). - **Contradictions are shown, never silently resolved.** Every finding shows both sides and the source page. - **Code calculates, agents read and talk.** Matching, maths and trust rules are plain code. Reading messy documents, judging impact, finding the approver and writing to people are agents. ## 3. Problems the system must find (verified against the raw data, 2026-11-21) | # | Problem | Evidence | Launch impact | Catch point | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | **Art books** | PO 8,000; goods receipt booked 80,000 "over delivery accepted"; delivery note scan shows 80,000 crossed out, 8,000 handwritten | ~5,900 Collector's copies short | After dock, before packing | | 2 | **Statues** | Inspection report: 9 of 125 defective, reject at 4; lot of 5,600 booked as unrestricted | 3,400 Collector's short unless a concession is signed (Category Lead post vacant) | After dock, before packing | | 3 | **Game cards** | PO 48,000; Korean shipping advice: 28,000 flown, 20,000 arrive 24 Nov. Modules never call each other directly; the UI reads the same state. ### Shared shapes (agree before coding, live in `src/ask_soony/schema.py`) ```text Claim { id, kind: quantity|date|status|revision|terms|iban|eta, part, po, po_line, shipment, supplier, value, unit, source_doc, page, quote, language, confidence, seen_at } Finding { id, kind: mismatch|stale|risk_news|forecast_late, claims: [claim ids], sides: [{source, value}], summary, part, created_at, status: open|resolved|dismissed } Impact { finding_id, part, units_short, copies_at_risk, edition, cell_hours_lost, deadline, slack_hours } Decision { finding_id, severity: call|email|notify|log, reason, approver, options: [{action, cost, effect}] } Action { id, decision_id, channel: call|email|portal, to, draft, trust: ask|allow_once|allow_always, status: draft|approved|sent|replied, reply } ``` ## 5. Who does what ### Jonas: watcher, criticality agent, calls and emails - **Watcher (in progress):** poll the portal, keep every file version, emit a change event per new or changed file. - **Criticality agent:** for each Finding + Impact, decide `call | email | notify | log`: - Code computes the hard numbers: copies at risk, Collector's cell hours lost (900/h), slack left before Sun 20:00 (all read from the plan and master data). - Agent judges what the code can't: is this a real risk or a false alarm (magnets), and who approves the fix. Reads the org chart and approval policy PP-07; if the approver post is vacant, finds the deputy or next level. - Output: a Decision with options, each with a cost and an effect ("accept Nowak rush offer: 8,000 books, Annex A price, truck arrives ~13 h after order"). - **Calls:** ElevenLabs voice call to the approver for `call` decisions: states the problem, the number, the options, and records the answer. - **Emails:** drafts to suppliers (from a registered address), internal notifications. Reads replies and turns them back into Claims. - **Trust gate:** nothing leaves for a supplier without a human click. "Allow once" / "allow always" per action type; internal notifications can be automatic sooner. - **Done when:** art books produce a call to the right person and an approved email to Nowak, live. ### Farhan: verification (three-way match) - **Claim extraction (agent):** every document becomes Claims, with source page and quote: order confirmations, shipping advice, delivery note scans (vision for handwriting), inspection reports, contracts, notices, price lists. Any language. - **Matching (code):** PO ↔ order confirmation ↔ goods receipt/delivery note, plus stock status ↔ inspection report and PO terms ↔ confirmation ↔ contract (Incoterms, price, IBAN). Emit a Finding for every disagreement with both sides. - **Rule checks on SAP alone (code):** e.g. received ≠ ordered by a large factor, stock booked unrestricted while an inspection exists. - **Done when:** findings #1, #2, #4, #5 come out of a fresh run over the portal data, with no part number in the code, and a new document in the portal produces new Claims without a code change. ### Lucas: arrival forecast (prediction) - **Will each open shipment and open PO line arrive in Hamburg before it is needed?** Use ETA + route transit (sea/air ETAs are at the port or FRA, so add the road leg from `routes.csv`) + shipping advice and confirmation claims + news. - **Rules, not a trained model.** About 25 open shipments and 30 hours left: too little history to train on, and rules are explainable on stage. Use past receipts only as a lateness signal per supplier and route if time allows. - **Silence detection:** flag shipments with no update for more than N hours, or past ETA and still "in delivery" (finding #6). - **News and notices:** turn news items and supplier notices into risk findings tagged by region, supplier and part; the criticality agent decides if they touch the launch (finding #7 must come out as "no launch risk"). - **Alternatives:** when a part won't arrive in time, list what can: stock elsewhere, other source on file, supplier offers in the notices (Nowak rush offer). - **Done when:** finding #3 and #6 come out of a fresh run, and the magnet drop is classified correctly. ### Akshat: platform, UI/UX, bringing it together - **One screen that answers:** "Will we make Sunday 20:00? What breaks first? What do I do now?" UI spec agreed 2026-11-22: - **User:** Felix (senior buyer). Decisions go to Maren when he escalates, or directly by rule: cost above the buyer limit, can stop a line, or a Collector's exception (read from PP-07 and the launch plan at runtime; each card states its reason). Maren's cards stay visible to Felix ("With Maren · called 21:14"). - **Shape:** a decision inbox, not a dashboard. The agents push (call / notification) with a deep link to one card; `/` = Felix's inbox, `/d/` = a single card (also the mobile view). No login. - **Layout:** status strip on top (per edition: status, copies at risk, slack hours, what breaks first, last portal drop); a 2D supply-chain map (~60%, left); a decision rail (~40%, right). - **Map:** d3-geo + world-atlas SVG, static, cropped from the US to Korea, no zoom. Nodes and legs come from the supplier profiles, `ports.csv`, `sites.csv` and `routes.csv` (SGSIN is missing: fall back to a generic sea path). Solid = air, dashed = sea. Colour = status: blue on track, amber at risk, red stops a line, grey pulsing silent. Shipments are placed by estimated position along the route (the GPS data is fake). A badge shows a node's open decisions. Munich is a faint dot. The map and the rail are linked both ways (click a route → filter cards; hover a card → highlight its route). - **Card:** headline with a number → deadline to decide → recommended option with its cost and effect (+1–2 alternatives) → **Approve · Edit · Escalate · Dismiss**; after the first approval of a routine type: "Send routine ETA chasers like this one automatically from now on? "What matters, and what does it cost?" | | **Felix Brunner** | Senior Buyer | Suppliers, trucks, stock, how things really run (not how the handbook says), the workarounds nobody wrote down | | **Nils Berger** | IT & Systems Lead | Data, files, exports, systems: "Why does this file look like that?" Precise questions only | - 3 blocks over the weekend. Times are announced in the portal and on Discord (the deep-dive slides listed Sat 14:00, Sat 17:00, Sun 09:00; the portal showed Block A at Sat 15:00). # Plan _Last updated: 2026-11-21. Owner of this file: Akshat. Read with [`docs/challenge.md`](docs/challenge.md) and [`strategy.md`](strategy.md)._ ## 1. The idea in one line > Soony's numbers are claims. We check them against every document, from order confirmation to delivery note, and act before the line stops. Soony's SAP and spreadsheets say the launch is fine. The documents that arrived (scans, PDFs in Korean, Chinese and Polish, inspection reports, supplier notices) say it is not. Nobody reads them in time. We do, we put a price on every gap in launch copies, and we get it to the person who can fix it: by call if it is urgent, otherwise by email or a notification. ## 2. Boundaries - **We work for the buyer (Soony).** We don't do procurement; we watch it and catch problems before they hit the launch. - **Buyer side only.** We read the data Soony already holds and decide on Soony's side. Suppliers are reached only by email from a registered sender address. No supplier or carrier system access (suppliers told us they refuse new tools). The supplier side is future scope. - **Not a second SAP.** A layer on top of Soony's systems that reads their exports and inboxes. - **Nothing hardcoded.** No supplier name, part number or quantity in code. Everything comes from the portal data at runtime. New and changed files must work without a code change, including format changes (e.g. `open_shipments.csv` → `.json`). - **Contradictions are shown, never silently resolved.** Every finding shows both sides and the source page. - **Code calculates, agents read and talk.** Matching, maths and trust rules are plain code. # Lighthouse

Our entry for the **Lio challenge "Keep the Line Running"** at START Hack Munich 2026.

Soony, a (fictional) games publisher, launches Grand Heist 6 on **Sunday 22 Nov, 20:00**. Every copy is packed in one distribution center in Hamburg, six suppliers deliver the parts, and the last 20% is not packed yet. Soony's data lives in SAP, spreadsheets, PDFs and scans, in four languages. Soony's head of procurement: "We find out at the dock."

We build agents that read that data, decide what is at risk and act on it before it is too late.

## What it is

**Lighthouse is an AI procurement team for the last mile of a launch.** Agents read everything the customer has (SAP exports, spreadsheets, supplier PDFs and scans in four languages, emails, news), find where the paperwork and the plan disagree, work out what that costs in copies and hours, and act: they write to suppliers, ask the warehouse, chase, and pass decisions to the person who signs. A human decides anything that costs money or changes the plan, with one tap.

Live: `https://ask-soony.stenglein.dev` (password protected; ask the team).

### Who uses it

| | Today | Launch | Sign-off page (phone) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **For** | The senior buyer, all day | The head of procurement, a few times a day | Whoever signs, when their phone buzzes |
| **Question** | What do I do now? | Will we make the deadline, what breaks first, who must decide? | Do I approve this? |

### The loop: notice → show → act → learn

1. **Notice.** Every portal change runs all checks within minutes. Documents are held against SAP (late or short, old revision, failed lot, goods receipt vs. delivery note), shipments are reconciled from every source (goods receipts, warehouse answers, supplier documents and replies, the hand-kept tracker, the system export), and silence is measured against the clock. Numbers that are only projections (a pack-out log hours old, book stock without a count) are called what they are.
2. **Show.** One calm decision at a time: the contradiction in one sentence, every number linked to the highlighted spot in its source document, what it means for the launch (when the packing line runs out of the part, how many copies that costs), and a recommendation with its price. Ranked by what the launch loses, not by which detector found it.
3. **Act.** Approve sends the email (reviewable: text, subject, recipient from known contacts only), asks the warehouse through a one-tap count page with photo OCR, or passes it on to the approver named in the approval policy, who answers on their phone. Supplier replies come back onto the case; confirmed orders become inbound with an estimated arrival; if it arrives too late to help, a follow-up decision appears. A voice assistant can talk a decision through and act only after a spoken yes.
4. **Learn.** After the second similar decision the system offers a routine. Routines start by asking (prepare, you send with one tap), then tell, then run quietly. Money and plan changes always come to a person.

### What makes it trustworthy

- **Nothing is hardcoded.** Products, parts, suppliers, sites, deadlines, shifts and policies are read from the data at runtime; files are recognised by their content, not their names.
- **Contradictions are shown, not resolved silently.** Every source keeps its age and its say.
- **The data can change shape.** A data check warns when a file can no longer be read, a column disappears, or a new kind of file arrives that nothing reads. Supplier master changes (status, contacts, bank details) become cases; a new address is never a send target without a human OK.
- **The mailbox is shared.** Emails sent by hand are read back from the Sent folder and tied to their case; sending the same thing twice needs a second click.

### Download the portal data once

Needs only `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN`, no LLM key:

```bash
uv run ask-soony download              # all current files into data/portal/, under their portal paths
uv run ask-soony download some/folder  # or into another folder
```

Run it again any time to bring the folder up to date: only new or changed files are fetched (the first run uses `archive.zip`). Files removed from the portal stay in the folder. Every version also lands in the version store (`data/store/`, see below). All of `data/` is gitignored: the data is confidential.

## Platform: decision inbox (`ask-soony run`)

One service: FastAPI serves the built UI (`web/dist`) and a JSON API over `data/state/`, and a background thread runs the watcher loop: poll the portal, mirror new files, record each new or changed file as a drop, and route the changed paths through the installed modules (`ask_soony.dispatch.refresh`: verifier and predictor). Missing modules or a failing step never stop the UI.

```bash
cd web && npm ci && npm run build && cd ..   # build the UI once
uv run ask-soony run --port 8000             # UI + API + watcher loop (needs SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN to poll)
uv run ask-soony serve --port 8000           # UI + API only, over the files already on disk
uv run ask-soony drop suppliers/<id>/notices/x.pdf [--from local.pdf]   # rehearse a live drop
uv run python scripts/seed_demo_state.py [--calm | --drop]   # dev only: placeholder state from the portal files
```

The UI reads the pipeline's `data/state/dispatch.json` (verifier decisions, editions, parts), the predictor's `data/state/impacts.json` and the shared shapes in `data/state/`. Source documents come from the image recognizer's readings: a frozen baseline committed in `src/ask_soony/verifier/baseline_sonnet/` (289 of 290 documents, so every clone has the art-book and statue findings without a run), plus `data/store/image_recognizer/` for new drops, read with `gpt-5.4-mini` (`python -m ask_soony.verifier.image_recognizer` reads only what the baseline lacks). A model change has to pass the gate first: `python -m ask_soony.verifier.image_recognizer.gate --model <model>` scores it on 11 hand-checked must-catch documents (see `src/ask_soony/verifier/image_recognizer/README.md`). Each ready message in a decision becomes an action; one that commits money goes to the policy's approver of exceptions, routine supplier questions stay with the buyer. The seed script is only a fallback when no pipeline output exists. Slack and the time a line stops come from the launch plan's shift table, read at runtime (`src/ask_soony/launch.py`). Clicks write only to `data/state/` (`actions.json`, `decision_status.json`, `trust.json`); nothing is sent from the UI.

### Deploy

`Dockerfile` builds the UI and runs `ask-soony run` on `$PORT`. No portal data is baked in; set `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN` (and an LLM key for the predictor) as secrets on the host. For example with Fly.io: `fly launch --no-deploy`, `fly secrets set SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN=REDACTED, `fly deploy`. Render: new Web Service from this repo, runtime Docker, same env vars.

## Data watcher (`src/ask_soony`)

A fixed loop polls the portal, keeps every file version and lets an LLM agent analyse each change.

1. **Poll** `GET /api/v1/files` and compare SHA-256 checksums. New or replaced files are downloaded (the first sync uses `archive.zip`) and stored by checksum under `data/store/blobs/`; nothing is overwritten.
2. **Log** every version, poll, analysis and finding in SQLite (`data/store/ask-soony.db`), so each finding points at the exact file version behind it.
3. **Analyse** each new or changed file with an agent. It reads the file (text, or page images for scans and photos), cross-checks other files with tools (`list_files`, `read_file`, `search_files`, `list_open_findings`) and submits a summary plus findings with evidence. Scans get a transcription that later searches can use.
4. **Notify** through console, macOS notifications, a Discord webhook or a generic JSON webhook.

To start the history from an earlier state, seed an empty store first: `uv run ask-soony import-snapshot data/archive.zip --at 2026-01-01T10:00:00+01:00` (a portal `archive.zip` or a folder with portal paths). Later polls then show every drop since that state.

The first poll stores the current state as a baseline without analysing it; only later changes are analysed. `analyze --path <prefix>` queues existing files on purpose.

```bash
uv run ask-soony download       # one-off: fetch everything into data/portal/ (no LLM needed)
uv run ask-soony poll           # one poll; the first one stores the baseline
uv run ask-soony analyze --path suppliers/SUP-0028_Karton_Nowak/notices/   # analyse chosen files
uv run ask-soony watch          # poll, analyse and notify every ASK_INTERVAL_SECONDS
uv run ask-soony refresh soony/erp/stock_snapshot.csv  # refresh verifier + decision cards
uv run ask-soony predict        # trace notices/news through the supply network
uv run ask-soony findings       # open findings
uv run ask-soony status
uv run pytest
```

### Dashboard: what changed, when

Every new or changed file version gets a "what changed" summary without any LLM: CSV files are compared row by row (rows added, removed, changed with old → new values; columns added, removed or renamed), Excel files cell by cell, everything else as a text diff. The dashboard shows each poll with its changes, every file's version history with diffs, the agent's findings and the supplier mail log (`data/outbox/`, `data/inbox/`).

```bash
uv run ask-soony watch-dashboard --interval 300 # poll every 5 min + dashboard on http://127.0.0.1:8765
uv run ask-soony dashboard              # dashboard only
```

The product runs as one server: the decision inbox app with the call webhooks (`/hooks/*`) and, with `ASK_BACKGROUND=on`, the portal watcher, alert escalation and the supplier reply poller as background loops:

```bash
(cd web && npm run build)
ASK_BACKGROUND=on uv run uvicorn ask_soony.api:app --port 8000
```

With `ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` set in the environment, the app asks for it on a login page (30-day cookie, so it works as a home screen app) or via basic auth; the call webhooks check their own signature or per-alert token instead.

Set `ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` in `.env` (HTTP basic auth, any user name). The dashboard listens on localhost only and refuses other addresses without a password. To share it, put a tunnel in front, for example a Cloudflare Tunnel with its own config file:

```yaml
# ~/.cloudflared/ask-soony.yml
protocol: http2            # QUIC is often blocked on event and campus networks
tunnel: <tunnel id>
credentials-file: /path/to/<tunnel id>.json
ingress:
  - hostname: ask-soony.example.com   # one level below the zone, so the free certificate covers it
    service: http://localhost:8765
  - service: http_status:404
```

```bash
cloudflared tunnel create ask-soony
cloudflared tunnel --config ~/.cloudflared/ask-soony.yml route dns <tunnel id> ask-soony.example.com
cloudflared tunnel --config ~/.cloudflared/ask-soony.yml run
```

Pass `--config` to `route dns` too: without it, `cloudflared` takes the tunnel from the default `config.yml` and may attach the hostname to a different tunnel.

### Alerts: notify, call, escalate

Other modules (verification, prediction, the watcher) raise alerts; the alert module decides how loud they get and who has to decide.

- **Criticality**: the producer sets a severity; with a deadline and `--impact launch` it is raised automatically (less than `critical_hours` left = critical, less than three times that = at least high).
- **Escalation policy** (`ASK_ALERT_POLICY`, default `data/alert-policy.json`, gitignored because it holds phone numbers; see `docs/alert-policy.example.json`): contacts, which channels each severity uses, the order of people to try and how many minutes each gets to decide before the next one is notified.
- **Channels**: dashboard (`/alerts`, with Approve / Escalate / Reject buttons), email (only with `ASK_ALERT_EMAIL=on`), call. Calls go through `ASK_CALL_PROVIDER`:
  - `dry_run` (default): logs what would be said, no credentials, no cost
  - `twilio`: reads the alert and takes a keypad answer (1 approve, 2 escalate, 3 reject), posted to `/hooks/twilio/<id>`. Needs `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID`, `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`, `TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER`. Works on a free Twilio trial: Twilio fetches the call script from `/hooks/twilio/twiml/<id>` (trials accept only a URL, not inline TwiML), uses the shared trial number shown under Voice → Try out Voice, and can only call verified numbers in the signup country
  - `openai`: Twilio calls the contact and hands the answered call to OpenAI's gpt-realtime over SIP (`<Dial><Sip>`). OpenAI posts `realtime.call.incoming` to `/hooks/openai` (signature-checked with `OPENAI_WEBHOOK_SECRET`); we accept with the alert as instructions and a `record_decision` function and follow the call on the sideband WebSocket. Needs `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_PROJECT_ID` and a project-level webhook (Settings → Project → Webhooks, event `realtime.call.incoming`). The model's sentences and the transcribed answers are logged in the alert history
  - `elevenlabs`: a voice agent talks the alert through. Needs `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID`, `ELEVENLABS_PHONE_NUMBER_ID` (a Twilio number imported into ElevenLabs)
- **Webhooks** need `ASK_PUBLIC_URL` (the tunnel). They bypass the dashboard password and are authenticated by a secret token per alert.

```bash
uv run ask-soony alert raise --severity high --impact launch --deadline 2026-01-10T06:00:00+01:00 \
  --title "Part short for launch" --message "5,900 missing" --action "Order 8,000 from supplier X"
uv run ask-soony alert list
uv run ask-soony alert decide 1 approve
uv run ask-soony watch-dashboard # also escalates undecided alerts every 30 seconds
```

ElevenLabs agent setup (dashboard): the call passes `contact_name`, `alert_id`, `alert_title`, `alert_message`, `proposed_action`, `deadline`, `decision_url` and `secret__alert_token` as dynamic variables. Use them in the prompt (for example "You are the procurement alert assistant. Tell {{contact_name}}: {{alert_title}}. {{alert_message}} Proposed action: {{proposed_action}}. Ask whether to approve, escalate or reject."), and add a server tool `record_decision` that POSTs JSON `{"alert_id": "{{alert_id}}", "decision": "<approve|escalate|reject>", "token": "{{secret__alert_token}}"}` to `{{decision_url}}`.

LLM backends (`ASK_LLM_PROVIDER`): `anthropic` (Claude via the Anthropic SDK, default `claude-opus-5-5`), `openai` (OpenAI), `llamacpp` (any OpenAI-compatible server, e.g. `llama-server --jinja` with `ASK_LLM_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080/v1`), `none` (poll and store only). Local models need vision support for scans.

## Change routing

All product code lives in `src/ask_soony/`. The watcher routes every new or changed portal
file through `verifier` and regenerates approval-gated decision cards. Changes under notices,
news, logistics, or shipments also run `predictor`. `dispatch` combines the refreshed results
into `data/state/dispatch.json`; it prepares notifications, emails, or calls for approval but
does not send external messages automatically.
## Run the dashboard locally

Prerequisites: [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Node 18 or newer.

```bash
scripts/dashboard.sh    # API on :8000, UI on http://localhost:5173, Ctrl-C stops both
```

It shows `web/fixtures/sample_state.json` (made-up data) until real output exists. To use real verifier output, run `uv run python -m verifier.act` on the verifier branch (it writes `data/store/decision_cards.json`, which the API picks up), or point `ASK_SOONY_STATE` at any file of that shape. Your clicks and the activity feed are stored in `data/state/` (gitignored).

## Data

All customer data comes from the Soony portal at runtime (`GET /api/v1/files`, `/api/v1/archive.zip`). It is confidential: use it only for this hackathon, never share it outside the team and never commit it (`data/` is gitignored).

# Lighthouse

Our entry for the **Lio challenge "Keep the Line Running"** at START Hack Munich 2026.

Soony, a (fictional) games publisher, launches Grand Heist 6 on **Sunday 22 Nov, 20:00**. Every copy is packed in one distribution center in Hamburg, six suppliers deliver the parts, and the last 20% is not packed yet. Soony's data lives in SAP, spreadsheets, PDFs and scans, in four languages. Soony's head of procurement: "We find out at the dock."

We build agents that read that data, decide what is at risk and act on it before it is too late.

4. Set up Entire so your agent sessions are tracked: see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#entire-session-tracking)

### Download the portal data once

Needs only `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN`, no LLM key:

```bash
uv run ask-soony download              # all current files into data/portal/, under their portal paths
uv run ask-soony download some/folder  # or into another folder
```

Run it again any time to bring the folder up to date: only new or changed files are fetched (the first run uses `archive.zip`). Files removed from the portal stay in the folder. Every version also lands in the version store (`data/store/`, see below). All of `data/` is gitignored: the data is confidential.

## Platform: decision inbox (`ask-soony run`)

One service: FastAPI serves the built UI (`web/dist`) and a JSON API over `data/state/`, and a background thread runs the watcher loop: poll the portal, mirror new files, record each new or changed file as a drop, and route the changed paths through the installed modules (`ask_soony.dispatch.refresh`: verifier and predictor). Missing modules or a failing step never stop the UI.

```bash
cd web && npm ci && npm run build && cd ..   # build the UI once
uv run ask-soony run --port 8000             # UI + API + watcher loop (needs SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN to poll)
uv run ask-soony serve --port 8000           # UI + API only, over the files already on disk
uv run ask-soony drop suppliers/<id>/notices/x.pdf [--from local.pdf]   # rehearse a live drop
uv run python scripts/seed_demo_state.py [--calm | --drop]   # dev only: placeholder state from the portal files
```

The UI reads the pipeline's `data/state/dispatch.json` (verifier decisions, editions, parts), the predictor's `data/state/impacts.json` and the shared shapes in `data/state/`. Source documents come from the image recognizer's readings: a frozen baseline committed in `src/ask_soony/verifier/baseline_sonnet/` (289 of 290 documents, so every clone has the art-book and statue findings without a run), plus `data/store/image_recognizer/` for new drops, read with `gpt-5.4-mini` (`python -m ask_soony.verifier.image_recognizer` reads only what the baseline lacks). A model change has to pass the gate first: `python -m ask_soony.verifier.image_recognizer.gate --model <model>` scores it on 11 hand-checked must-catch documents (see `src/ask_soony/verifier/image_recognizer/README.md`). Each ready message in a decision becomes an action; one that commits money goes to the policy's approver of exceptions, routine supplier questions stay with the buyer. The seed script is only a fallback when no pipeline output exists. Slack and the time a line stops come from the launch plan's shift table, read at runtime (`src/ask_soony/launch.py`). Clicks write only to `data/state/` (`actions.json`, `decision_status.json`, `trust.json`); nothing is sent from the UI.

### Deploy

`Dockerfile` builds the UI and runs `ask-soony run` on `$PORT`. No portal data is baked in; set `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN` (and an LLM key for the predictor) as secrets on the host. For example with Fly.io: `fly launch --no-deploy`, `fly secrets set SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN=REDACTED, `fly deploy`. Render: new Web Service from this repo, runtime Docker, same env vars.

## Data watcher (`src/ask_soony`)

A fixed loop polls the portal, keeps every file version and lets an LLM agent analyse each change.

1. **Poll** `GET /api/v1/files` and compare SHA-256 checksums. New or replaced files are downloaded (the first sync uses `archive.zip`) and stored by checksum under `data/store/blobs/`; nothing is overwritten.
2. **Log** every version, poll, analysis and finding in SQLite (`data/store/ask-soony.db`), so each finding points at the exact file version behind it.
3. **Analyse** each new or changed file with an agent. It reads the file (text, or page images for scans and photos), cross-checks other files with tools (`list_files`, `read_file`, `search_files`, `list_open_findings`) and submits a summary plus findings with evidence. Scans get a transcription that later searches can use.
4. **Notify** through console, macOS notifications, a Discord webhook or a generic JSON webhook.

To start the history from an earlier state, seed an empty store first: `uv run ask-soony import-snapshot data/archive.zip --at 2026-01-01T10:00:00+01:00` (a portal `archive.zip` or a folder with portal paths). Later polls then show every drop since that state.

The first poll stores the current state as a baseline without analysing it; only later changes are analysed. `analyze --path <prefix>` queues existing files on purpose.

```bash
uv run ask-soony download       # one-off: fetch everything into data/portal/ (no LLM needed)
uv run ask-soony poll           # one poll; the first one stores the baseline
uv run ask-soony analyze --path suppliers/SUP-0028_Karton_Nowak/notices/   # analyse chosen files
uv run ask-soony watch          # poll, analyse and notify every ASK_INTERVAL_SECONDS
uv run ask-soony refresh soony/erp/stock_snapshot.csv  # refresh verifier + decision cards
uv run ask-soony predict        # trace notices/news through the supply network
uv run ask-soony findings       # open findings
uv run ask-soony status
uv run pytest
```

### Dashboard: what changed, when

Every new or changed file version gets a "what changed" summary without any LLM: CSV files are compared row by row (rows added, removed, changed with old → new values; columns added, removed or renamed), Excel files cell by cell, everything else as a text diff. The dashboard shows each poll with its changes, every file's version history with diffs, the agent's findings and the supplier mail log (`data/outbox/`, `data/inbox/`).

```bash
uv run ask-soony watch-dashboard --interval 300 # poll every 5 min + dashboard on http://127.0.0.1:8765
uv run ask-soony dashboard              # dashboard only
```

The product runs as one server: the decision inbox app with the call webhooks (`/hooks/*`) and, with `ASK_BACKGROUND=on`, the portal watcher, alert escalation and the supplier reply poller as background loops:

```bash
(cd web && npm run build)
ASK_BACKGROUND=on uv run uvicorn ask_soony.api:app --port 8000
```

With `ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` set in the environment, the app asks for it on a login page (30-day cookie, so it works as a home screen app) or via basic auth; the call webhooks check their own signature or per-alert token instead.

Set `ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` in `.env` (HTTP basic auth, any user name). The dashboard listens on localhost only and refuses other addresses without a password. To share it, put a tunnel in front, for example a Cloudflare Tunnel with its own config file:

```yaml
# ~/.cloudflared/ask-soony.yml
protocol: http2            # QUIC is often blocked on event and campus networks
tunnel: <tunnel id>
credentials-file: /path/to/<tunnel id>.json
ingress:
  - hostname: ask-soony.example.com   # one level below the zone, so the free certificate covers it
    service: http://localhost:8765
  - service: http_status:404
```

```bash
cloudflared tunnel create ask-soony
cloudflared tunnel --config ~/.cloudflared/ask-soony.yml route dns <tunnel id> ask-soony.example.com
cloudflared tunnel --config ~/.cloudflared/ask-soony.yml run
```

Pass `--config` to `route dns` too: without it, `cloudflared` takes the tunnel from the default `config.yml` and may attach the hostname to a different tunnel.

### Alerts: notify, call, escalate

Other modules (verification, prediction, the watcher) raise alerts; the alert module decides how loud they get and who has to decide.

- **Criticality**: the producer sets a severity; with a deadline and `--impact launch` it is raised automatically (less than `critical_hours` left = critical, less than three times that = at least high).
- **Escalation policy** (`ASK_ALERT_POLICY`, default `data/alert-policy.json`, gitignored because it holds phone numbers; see `docs/alert-policy.example.json`): contacts, which channels each severity uses, the order of people to try and how many minutes each gets to decide before the next one is notified.
- **Channels**: dashboard (`/alerts`, with Approve / Escalate / Reject buttons), email (only with `ASK_ALERT_EMAIL=on`), call. Calls go through `ASK_CALL_PROVIDER`:
  - `dry_run` (default): logs what would be said, no credentials, no cost
  - `twilio`: reads the alert and takes a keypad answer (1 approve, 2 escalate, 3 reject), posted to `/hooks/twilio/<id>`. Needs `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID`, `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`, `TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER`. Works on a free Twilio trial: Twilio fetches the call script from `/hooks/twilio/twiml/<id>` (trials accept only a URL, not inline TwiML), uses the shared trial number shown under Voice → Try out Voice, and can only call verified numbers in the signup country
  - `openai`: Twilio calls the contact and hands the answered call to OpenAI's gpt-realtime over SIP (`<Dial><Sip>`). OpenAI posts `realtime.call.incoming` to `/hooks/openai` (signature-checked with `OPENAI_WEBHOOK_SECRET`); we accept with the alert as instructions and a `record_decision` function and follow the call on the sideband WebSocket. Needs `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_PROJECT_ID` and a project-level webhook (Settings → Project → Webhooks, event `realtime.call.incoming`). The model's sentences and the transcribed answers are logged in the alert history
  - `elevenlabs`: a voice agent talks the alert through. Needs `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID`, `ELEVENLABS_PHONE_NUMBER_ID` (a Twilio number imported into ElevenLabs)
- **Webhooks** need `ASK_PUBLIC_URL` (the tunnel). They bypass the dashboard password and are authenticated by a secret token per alert.

```bash
uv run ask-soony alert raise --severity high --impact launch --deadline 2026-01-10T06:00:00+01:00 \
  --title "Part short for launch" --message "5,900 missing" --action "Order 8,000 from supplier X"
uv run ask-soony alert list
uv run ask-soony alert decide 1 approve
uv run ask-soony watch-dashboard # also escalates undecided alerts every 30 seconds
```

ElevenLabs agent setup (dashboard): the call passes `contact_name`, `alert_id`, `alert_title`, `alert_message`, `proposed_action`, `deadline`, `decision_url` and `secret__alert_token` as dynamic variables. Use them in the prompt (for example "You are the procurement alert assistant. Tell {{contact_name}}: {{alert_title}}. {{alert_message}} Proposed action: {{proposed_action}}. Ask whether to approve, escalate or reject."), and add a server tool `record_decision` that POSTs JSON `{"alert_id": "{{alert_id}}", "decision": "<approve|escalate|reject>", "token": "{{secret__alert_token}}"}` to `{{decision_url}}`.

LLM backends (`ASK_LLM_PROVIDER`): `anthropic` (Claude via the Anthropic SDK, default `claude-opus-5-5`), `openai` (OpenAI), `llamacpp` (any OpenAI-compatible server, e.g. `llama-server --jinja` with `ASK_LLM_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080/v1`), `none` (poll and store only). Local models need vision support for scans.

## Change routing

All product code lives in `src/ask_soony/`. The watcher routes every new or changed portal
file through `verifier` and regenerates approval-gated decision cards. Changes under notices,
news, logistics, or shipments also run `predictor`. `dispatch` combines the refreshed results
into `data/state/dispatch.json`; it prepares notifications, emails, or calls for approval but
does not send external messages automatically.
## Run the dashboard locally

Prerequisites: [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Node 18 or newer.

```bash
scripts/dashboard.sh    # API on :8000, UI on http://localhost:5173, Ctrl-C stops both
```

It shows `web/fixtures/sample_state.json` (made-up data) until real output exists. To use real verifier output, run `uv run python -m verifier.act` on the verifier branch (it writes `data/store/decision_cards.json`, which the API picks up), or point `ASK_SOONY_STATE` at any file of that shape. Your clicks and the activity feed are stored in `data/state/` (gitignored).

## Data

All customer data comes from the Soony portal at runtime (`GET /api/v1/files`, `/api/v1/archive.zip`). It is confidential: use it only for this hackathon, never share it outside the team and never commit it (`data/` is gitignored).
