+# Lighthouse
+
+Lighthouse is our entry for the **Lio "Keep the Line Running"** challenge at START Hack Munich 2026. It is an AI-assisted launch-control system for Soony, a fictional games publisher preparing to ship *Grand Heist 6*.
+
+Soony's source of truth is scattered across ERP exports, spreadsheets, PDFs, scans, supplier correspondence, and logistics data. Lighthouse treats every number as a claim: it checks the claim against its evidence, calculates the packing impact, and puts an approval-gated next action in front of the person who can make it happen.
+
+> Customer and portal data are confidential hackathon material. Fetch them only through the portal API, keep them in the gitignored `data/` directory, and do not share or commit them.
+
+## What it does
+
+- Watches the portal for new or changed files, preserving each observed version by checksum.
+- Reads changing, imperfect data layouts rather than relying on supplier-specific file names or hard-coded launch quantities.
+- Links purchase orders, confirmations, shipping information, goods receipts, stock, and document readings; it preserves disagreements instead of silently choosing a side.
+- Calculates usable stock, incoming supply, shortfalls, packing slack, and the time a packing line will run dry.
+- Uses an LLM-backed event-impact agent to trace relevant notices, news, logistics, and shipment changes through the supply network.
+- Presents evidence-backed decision cards in a React decision inbox, plus launch, supplier, routine, history, warehouse-count, and sign-off views.
+- Keeps actions human-approved: an approved supplier email is sent only to a known supplier contact; decisions, replies, sign-offs, and any resulting commitments remain attached to the card.
+- Supports optional push notifications, Teams messages, escalation calls, voice-assisted decisions, shared-mailbox reconciliation, and controlled routines.
+
+## Architecture
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart LR
+  Portal[Soony portal API] --> Watcher[Portal watcher]
+  Watcher --> Store[Version store and portal mirror]
+  Store --> Verify[Verifier and shortfall calculation]
+  Store --> Predict[Event-impact agent]
+  Verify --> State[data/state]
+  Predict --> State
+  State --> API[FastAPI state API]
+  API --> UI[React decision inbox]
+  UI --> Approval[Human approval or sign-off]
+  Approval --> Action[Known-contact email, warehouse request, or escalation]
+  Action --> State
+```
+
+The portal watcher stores raw versions in `data/store/` and mirrors current files to `data/portal/`. The dispatch pipeline writes its combined verification payload to `data/state/dispatch.json`; the impact agent writes event analyses to `data/state/event_impacts.json`. The API combines those files with the current portal mirror at request time, so a missing or failed optional module does not take down the inbox.
+
+`data/` is deliberately gitignored. The committed image-recognizer baseline under `src/ask_soony/verifier/baseline_sonnet/` supplies vetted readings for the original document set; readings for new portal documents stay in `data/store/image_recognizer/`.

+## Technology
+
+| Layer | Implementation |
+| --- | --- |
+| Service and CLI | Python 3.13+, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic |
+| Data and documents | SQLite, pandas, openpyxl, pypdf/pypdfium2, Pillow, Tesseract in the container |
+| Agents | Anthropic, OpenAI, or an OpenAI-compatible local endpoint such as llama.cpp |
+| Web app | React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Radix UI, D3/TopoJSON |
+| Delivery | Docker multi-stage build: Vite frontend plus Python service |

+
+| Location | Responsibility |
+| --- | --- |
+| `src/ask_soony/cli.py` | `ask-soony` command-line entry point |
+| `src/ask_soony/watcher.py`, `store.py`, `portal.py` | Portal polling, immutable version storage, and portal API access |
+| `src/ask_soony/dispatch/`, `verifier/` | Document/ERP linking, contradiction checks, shortfall calculation, and decision payloads |
+| `src/ask_soony/predictor/` | LLM-assisted impact analysis for notices, news, logistics, and shipments |
+| `src/ask_soony/api.py` | FastAPI application, state composition, approval endpoints, and built-UI serving |
+| `src/ask_soony/cardtools.py`, `replies.py`, `outbox.py` | Approved email delivery, supplier-reply matching, and sent-mail reconciliation |
+| `src/ask_soony/alerts.py`, `calls.py`, `push.py`, `teams.py` | Optional notification, escalation, call, push, and Teams integrations |
+| `src/ask_soony/routines.py` | Approval-aware, sandboxed repeatable actions |
+| `web/src/` | Live React decision-inbox UI |
+| `web/globe/` | Parked earlier globe prototype; it is not the live UI |
+| `tests/`, `src/ask_soony/verifier/**/tests/` | API, workflow, routing, verification, and impact tests |

+

+
+```bash

+uv sync --group dev
+
+cp .env.example .env

+```

+| Need | Required settings |
+| --- | --- |
+| Download/poll the Soony portal | `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN` |
+| Anthropic-backed analysis (default) | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
+| OpenAI-backed analysis | `ASK_LLM_PROVIDER=openai`, plus `ASK_LLM_API_KEY` or an environment-discovered OpenAI key |

+| Run without model calls | `ASK_LLM_PROVIDER=none` |
+| Protect the web app | `ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` |
+| Send and reconcile supplier mail | `ASK_MAIL_ADDRESS`, `ASK_MAIL_PASSWORD`, `ASK_SMTP_HOST`, and `ASK_IMAP_HOST` |
+| Run optional background integrations | `ASK_BACKGROUND=on`; configure the relevant push, Teams, call, or alert settings from `.env.example` |
+

+
+## Run locally
+
+Build the frontend before using the Python server; FastAPI serves `web/dist` when it exists.

+### Decision inbox over existing local state
+
+```bash
+uv run ask-soony serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
+```
+
+Open <http://127.0.0.1:8000>. This starts the UI and API only; it does not poll the portal. It is useful for inspecting an existing portal mirror and state directory.
+
+### Decision inbox with portal polling and pipeline refresh
+
+```bash
+uv run ask-soony run --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
+```
+
+This starts the same web service and a background portal loop. Each first poll establishes a baseline; later new or changed paths are recorded as events and routed through verification. Notices, news, logistics, and shipment changes are also eligible for impact prediction when an LLM backend is configured. The polling period defaults to 300 seconds and can be changed with `ASK_INTERVAL_SECONDS` or `--interval`.
+
+For frontend development with Vite hot reload, use:
+
+```bash
+scripts/dashboard.sh
+```
+
+That starts the API on port 8000 and Vite on <http://localhost:5173>, proxying `/api` to the service.
+
+## Portal and analysis commands
+
+All commands are available through `uv run ask-soony --help`.
+
+```bash
+# Fetch the current portal state into data/portal/ and record it in the version store.
+uv run ask-soony download
+
+# Record one portal poll. The first poll is a baseline by default.
+uv run ask-soony poll
+
+# Queue stored files under a path and process them with the configured analyst.
+uv run ask-soony analyze --path suppliers/<supplier-id>/notices/
+
+# Poll, analyse, notify, and refresh the pipeline in a terminal loop.
+uv run ask-soony watch

+# Recompute pipeline output from files already in the local mirror.

+# Run or inspect event-impact analysis.
+uv run ask-soony predict
+uv run ask-soony predict --list

+# Rehearse a new portal drop against the local mirror.

+uv run ask-soony findings
+```
+
+`ask-soony download`, `poll`, `watch`, and `run` need `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN`. `analyze` and LLM-backed `predict` need a configured model provider. `ASK_LLM_PROVIDER=none` leaves portal storage and deterministic verification available while disabling model calls.
+
+## Safety and action model
+
+Lighthouse is designed to act without bypassing people or evidence:
+
+- A decision card retains the contradictory sources and evidence anchors that produced it.
+- UI actions are recorded in state first. An approved email is deliverable only to a contact trusted from the supplier master data or an existing matched reply; arbitrary typed recipients are rejected.
+- Supplier replies are matched back to prior sent messages by email thread (with a conservative subject fallback), then recorded on the originating decision.
+- The shared mailbox's Sent folder can be reconciled so manually sent supplier messages are visible before another draft is sent.
+- Repeated work can become a routine, but routines are sandboxed and use a trust ladder. Actions that cost money or change the plan remain approval-gated.
+- Call, push, Teams, and email integrations are optional. The default call provider is `dry_run`.
+
+## Tests and checks
+
+```bash

+uv run pytest -q
+
+# Python lint
+uv run ruff check .
+
+# Type-check and production-build the web app

+
+# Run the configured web linter

+```
+
+The test suite uses temporary fixtures and is designed not to load a developer's real `.env` file.
+

+
+The included `Dockerfile` builds the Vite app and starts the combined service with:
+
+```text
+ask-soony run --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT
+```
+
+Build and run it locally:
+
+```bash
+docker build -t lighthouse .
+docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 \
+  -e SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN \
+  -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY \
+  -e ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD \
+  lighthouse
+```
+

At minimum, a polling deployment needs `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN`; add a model key only for LLM-backed analysis. Set `ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` before exposing the dashboard beyond a trusted network.
+
+## Challenge context
+
+The product problem, constraints, and expected deliverables are in [docs/challenge.md](docs/challenge.md). The team’s current product and module plan is in [plan.md](plan.md); [strategy.md](strategy.md) records the narrower verification-first rationale.
+
+For repository workflow and agent instructions, read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

# Lighthouse

Our entry for the **Lio challenge "Keep the Line Running"** at START Hack Munich 2026.

Soony, a (fictional) games publisher, launches Grand Heist 6 on **Sunday 22 Nov, 20:00**. Every copy is packed in one distribution center in Hamburg, six suppliers deliver the parts, and the last 20% is not packed yet. Soony's data lives in SAP, spreadsheets, PDFs and scans, in four languages. Soony's head of procurement: "We find out at the dock."

We build agents that read that data, decide what is at risk and act on it before it is too late.

## What it is

**Lighthouse is an AI procurement team for the last mile of a launch.** Agents read everything the customer has (SAP exports, spreadsheets, supplier PDFs and scans in four languages, emails, news), find where the paperwork and the plan disagree, work out what that costs in copies and hours, and act: they write to suppliers, ask the warehouse, chase, and pass decisions to the person who signs. A human decides anything that costs money or changes the plan, with one tap.

Live: `https://ask-soony.stenglein.dev` (password protected; ask the team).

### Who uses it

| | Today | Launch | Sign-off page (phone) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **For** | The senior buyer, all day | The head of procurement, a few times a day | Whoever signs, when their phone buzzes |
| **Question** | What do I do now? | Will we make the deadline, what breaks first, who must decide? | Do I approve this? |

### The loop: notice → show → act → learn

1. **Notice.** Every portal change runs all checks within minutes. Documents are held against SAP (late or short, old revision, failed lot, goods receipt vs. delivery note), shipments are reconciled from every source (goods receipts, warehouse answers, supplier documents and replies, the hand-kept tracker, the system export), and silence is measured against the clock. Numbers that are only projections (a pack-out log hours old, book stock without a count) are called what they are.
2. **Show.** One calm decision at a time: the contradiction in one sentence, every number linked to the highlighted spot in its source document, what it means for the launch (when the packing line runs out of the part, how many copies that costs), and a recommendation with its price. Ranked by what the launch loses, not by which detector found it.
3. **Act.** Approve sends the email (reviewable: text, subject, recipient from known contacts only), asks the warehouse through a one-tap count page with photo OCR, or passes it on to the approver named in the approval policy, who answers on their phone. Supplier replies come back onto the case; confirmed orders become inbound with an estimated arrival; if it arrives too late to help, a follow-up decision appears. A voice assistant can talk a decision through and act only after a spoken yes.
4. **Learn.** After the second similar decision the system offers a routine. Routines start by asking (prepare, you send with one tap), then tell, then run quietly. Money and plan changes always come to a person.

### What makes it trustworthy

- **Nothing is hardcoded.** Products, parts, suppliers, sites, deadlines, shifts and policies are read from the data at runtime; files are recognised by their content, not their names.
- **Contradictions are shown, not resolved silently.** Every source keeps its age and its say.
- **The data can change shape.** A data check warns when a file can no longer be read, a column disappears, or a new kind of file arrives that nothing reads. Supplier master changes (status, contacts, bank details) become cases; a new address is never a send target without a human OK.
- **The mailbox is shared.** Emails sent by hand are read back from the Sent folder and tied to their case; sending the same thing twice needs a second click.

### Where it lives

| Area | Code |
|---|---|
| Server, state, ranking, sign-off routing | `src/ask_soony/api.py`, `signoff.py` |
| Document vs. ERP checks, grounding | `papercheck.py`, `anchors.py`, `verifier/` |
| Launch clock, editions, parts, inbound | `launch.py`, `launch_view.py`, `commitments.py`, `tracking.py` |
| Asking the warehouse (counts, arrivals) | `floor.py` |
| Supplier email, replies, shared mailbox | `cardtools.py`, `replies.py`, `outbox.py` |
| Routines (sandboxed, trust ladder) | `routines.py` |
| Data shape and master data checks | `datacheck.py`, `supplier_master.py`, `memo.py` |
| Voice, push, Teams, calls | `voice.py`, `push.py`, `teams.py`, `calls.py` |
| UI (React, Tailwind) | `web/src/components/` (`Today`, `Launch`, `Routines`, `SupplyMap`, `CountPage`, `OkPage`) |

Tests: `uv run pytest -q`. UI: `cd web && npm run build`.

**Demo instance** (`scripts/demo.sh reset`): a second server on `:8001` (`ask-soony-demo.stenglein.dev`) with every case open again and no real supplier email (`ASK_MAIL_DRY=on` records mails in `dry_outbox.json`). Push still reaches subscribed phones, so the count page and the sign-off page can be shown. Run `reset` between rehearsals; `snapshot` rebuilds it from the live state.

## Getting started

1. Clone the repo and install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), then `uv sync --group dev`
2. Create your `.env` from the template: `cp .env.example .env`. It is gitignored; never commit it or paste keys in chat.
3. Put the keys into `.env`:

   | Variable | Where to get it | Needed for |
   |---|---|---|
   | `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN` | Portal → Settings → API token | Everything (download, poll, watch) |
   | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | [Claude Console](https://console.anthropic.com/) → API keys | `analyze` and `watch` with the default Claude backend |
   | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | [OpenAI Platform](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys) → API keys | Reading new documents (image recognizer, `gpt-5.4-mini`) |
   | `ASK_LLM_PROVIDER` + `ASK_LLM_API_KEY` | OpenAI key, or empty for a local llama.cpp server | Only if you use another backend (see below) |

   `SOONY_PORTAL_URL` is already filled in by the template.
4. Set up Entire so your agent sessions are tracked: see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#entire-session-tracking)

### Download the portal data once

Needs only `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN`, no LLM key:

```bash
uv run ask-soony download              # all current files into data/portal/, under their portal paths
uv run ask-soony download some/folder  # or into another folder
```

Run it again any time to bring the folder up to date: only new or changed files are fetched (the first run uses `archive.zip`). Files removed from the portal stay in the folder. Every version also lands in the version store (`data/store/`, see below). All of `data/` is gitignored: the data is confidential.

## Platform: decision inbox (`ask-soony run`)

One service: FastAPI serves the built UI (`web/dist`) and a JSON API over `data/state/`, and a background thread runs the watcher loop: poll the portal, mirror new files, record each new or changed file as a drop, and route the changed paths through the installed modules (`ask_soony.dispatch.refresh`: verifier and predictor). Missing modules or a failing step never stop the UI.

```bash
cd web && npm ci && npm run build && cd ..   # build the UI once
uv run ask-soony run --port 8000             # UI + API + watcher loop (needs SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN to poll)
uv run ask-soony serve --port 8000           # UI + API only, over the files already on disk
uv run ask-soony drop suppliers/<id>/notices/x.pdf [--from local.pdf]   # rehearse a live drop
uv run python scripts/seed_demo_state.py [--calm | --drop]   # dev only: placeholder state from the portal files
```

The UI reads the pipeline's `data/state/dispatch.json` (verifier decisions, editions, parts), the predictor's `data/state/impacts.json` and the shared shapes in `data/state/`. Source documents come from the image recognizer's readings: a frozen baseline committed in `src/ask_soony/verifier/baseline_sonnet/` (289 of 290 documents, so every clone has the art-book and statue findings without a run), plus `data/store/image_recognizer/` for new drops, read with `gpt-5.4-mini` (`python -m ask_soony.verifier.image_recognizer` reads only what the baseline lacks). A model change has to pass the gate first: `python -m ask_soony.verifier.image_recognizer.gate --model <model>` scores it on 11 hand-checked must-catch documents (see `src/ask_soony/verifier/image_recognizer/README.md`). Each ready message in a decision becomes an action; one that commits money goes to the policy's approver of exceptions, routine supplier questions stay with the buyer. The seed script is only a fallback when no pipeline output exists. Slack and the time a line stops come from the launch plan's shift table, read at runtime (`src/ask_soony/launch.py`). Clicks write only to `data/state/` (`actions.json`, `decision_status.json`, `trust.json`); nothing is sent from the UI.

### Deploy

`Dockerfile` builds the UI and runs `ask-soony run` on `$PORT`. No portal data is baked in; set `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN` (and an LLM key for the predictor) as secrets on the host. For example with Fly.io: `fly launch --no-deploy`, `fly secrets set SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN=REDACTED, `fly deploy`. Render: new Web Service from this repo, runtime Docker, same env vars.

## Data watcher (`src/ask_soony`)

A fixed loop polls the portal, keeps every file version and lets an LLM agent analyse each change.

1. **Poll** `GET /api/v1/files` and compare SHA-256 checksums. New or replaced files are downloaded (the first sync uses `archive.zip`) and stored by checksum under `data/store/blobs/`; nothing is overwritten.
2. **Log** every version, poll, analysis and finding in SQLite (`data/store/ask-soony.db`), so each finding points at the exact file version behind it.
3. **Analyse** each new or changed file with an agent. It reads the file (text, or page images for scans and photos), cross-checks other files with tools (`list_files`, `read_file`, `search_files`, `list_open_findings`) and submits a summary plus findings with evidence. Scans get a transcription that later searches can use.
4. **Notify** through console, macOS notifications, a Discord webhook or a generic JSON webhook.

To start the history from an earlier state, seed an empty store first: `uv run ask-soony import-snapshot data/archive.zip --at 2026-01-01T10:00:00+01:00` (a portal `archive.zip` or a folder with portal paths). Later polls then show every drop since that state.

The first poll stores the current state as a baseline without analysing it; only later changes are analysed. `analyze --path <prefix>` queues existing files on purpose.

```bash
uv run ask-soony download       # one-off: fetch everything into data/portal/ (no LLM needed)
uv run ask-soony poll           # one poll; the first one stores the baseline
uv run ask-soony analyze --path suppliers/SUP-0028_Karton_Nowak/notices/   # analyse chosen files
uv run ask-soony watch          # poll, analyse and notify every ASK_INTERVAL_SECONDS
uv run ask-soony refresh soony/erp/stock_snapshot.csv  # refresh verifier + decision cards
uv run ask-soony predict        # trace notices/news through the supply network
uv run ask-soony findings       # open findings
uv run ask-soony status
uv run pytest
```

### Dashboard: what changed, when

Every new or changed file version gets a "what changed" summary without any LLM: CSV files are compared row by row (rows added, removed, changed with old → new values; columns added, removed or renamed), Excel files cell by cell, everything else as a text diff. The dashboard shows each poll with its changes, every file's version history with diffs, the agent's findings and the supplier mail log (`data/outbox/`, `data/inbox/`).

```bash
uv run ask-soony watch-dashboard --interval 300 # poll every 5 min + dashboard on http://127.0.0.1:8765
uv run ask-soony dashboard              # dashboard only
```

The product runs as one server: the decision inbox app with the call webhooks (`/hooks/*`) and, with `ASK_BACKGROUND=on`, the portal watcher, alert escalation and the supplier reply poller as background loops:

```bash
(cd web && npm run build)
ASK_BACKGROUND=on uv run uvicorn ask_soony.api:app --port 8000
```

With `ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` set in the environment, the app asks for it on a login page (30-day cookie, so it works as a home screen app) or via basic auth; the call webhooks check their own signature or per-alert token instead.

Set `ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` in `.env` (HTTP basic auth, any user name). The dashboard listens on localhost only and refuses other addresses without a password. To share it, put a tunnel in front, for example a Cloudflare Tunnel with its own config file:

```yaml
# ~/.cloudflared/ask-soony.yml
protocol: http2            # QUIC is often blocked on event and campus networks
tunnel: <tunnel id>
credentials-file: /path/to/<tunnel id>.json
ingress:
  - hostname: ask-soony.example.com   # one level below the zone, so the free certificate covers it
    service: http://localhost:8765
  - service: http_status:404
```

```bash
cloudflared tunnel create ask-soony
cloudflared tunnel --config ~/.cloudflared/ask-soony.yml route dns <tunnel id> ask-soony.example.com
cloudflared tunnel --config ~/.cloudflared/ask-soony.yml run
```

Pass `--config` to `route dns` too: without it, `cloudflared` takes the tunnel from the default `config.yml` and may attach the hostname to a different tunnel.

### Alerts: notify, call, escalate

Other modules (verification, prediction, the watcher) raise alerts; the alert module decides how loud they get and who has to decide.

- **Criticality**: the producer sets a severity; with a deadline and `--impact launch` it is raised automatically (less than `critical_hours` left = critical, less than three times that = at least high).

  - `dry_run` (default): logs what would be said, no credentials, no cost
  - `twilio`: reads the alert and takes a keypad answer (1 approve, 2 escalate, 3 reject), posted to `/hooks/twilio/<id>`. Needs `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID`, `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`, `TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER`. The model's sentences and the transcribed answers are logged in the alert history
  - `elevenlabs`: a voice agent talks the alert through. Needs `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID`, `ELEVENLABS_PHONE_NUMBER_ID` (a Twilio number imported into ElevenLabs)

```bash
uv run ask-soony alert raise --severity high --impact launch --deadline 2026-01-10T06:00:00+01:00 \
  --title "Part short for launch" --message "5,900 missing" --action "Order 8,000 from supplier X"

uv run ask-soony alert decide 1 approve
uv run ask-soony watch-dashboard # also escalates undecided alerts every 30 seconds

Use them in the prompt (for example "You are the procurement alert assistant. Tell {{contact_name}}: {{alert_title}}. {{alert_message}} Proposed action: {{proposed_action}}. # Lighthouse

Lighthouse is our entry for the **Lio "Keep the Line Running"** challenge at START Hack Munich 2026. It is an AI-assisted launch-control system for Soony, a fictional games publisher preparing to ship *Grand Heist 6*.

Soony's source of truth is scattered across ERP exports, spreadsheets, PDFs, scans, supplier correspondence, and logistics data. Lighthouse treats every number as a claim: it checks the claim against its evidence, calculates the packing impact, and puts an approval-gated next action in front of the person who can make it happen.

> Customer and portal data are confidential hackathon material. Fetch them only through the portal API, keep them in the gitignored `data/` directory, and do not share or commit them.

## What it does

- Watches the portal for new or changed files, preserving each observed version by checksum.
- Reads changing, imperfect data layouts rather than relying on supplier-specific file names or hard-coded launch quantities.
- Links purchase orders, confirmations, shipping information, goods receipts, stock, and document readings; it preserves disagreements instead of silently choosing a side.
- Calculates usable stock, incoming supply, shortfalls, packing slack, and the time a packing line will run dry.
- Uses an LLM-backed event-impact agent to trace relevant notices, news, logistics, and shipment changes through the supply network.
- Presents evidence-backed decision cards in a React decision inbox, plus launch, supplier, routine, history, warehouse-count, and sign-off views.
- Keeps actions human-approved: an approved supplier email is sent only to a known supplier contact; decisions, replies, sign-offs, and any resulting commitments remain attached to the card.
- Supports optional push notifications, Teams messages, escalation calls, voice-assisted decisions, shared-mailbox reconciliation, and controlled routines.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Portal[Soony portal API] --> Watcher[Portal watcher]
  Watcher --> Store[Version store and portal mirror]
  Store --> Verify[Verifier and shortfall calculation]
  Store --> Predict[Event-impact agent]
  Verify --> State[data/state]
  Predict --> State
  State --> API[FastAPI state API]
  API --> UI[React decision inbox]
  UI --> Approval[Human approval or sign-off]
  Approval --> Action[Known-contact email, warehouse request, or escalation]
  Action --> State
```

The portal watcher stores raw versions in `data/store/` and mirrors current files to `data/portal/`. The dispatch pipeline writes its combined verification payload to `data/state/dispatch.json`; the impact agent writes event analyses to `data/state/event_impacts.json`. The API combines those files with the current portal mirror at request time, so a missing or failed optional module does not take down the inbox.

`data/` is deliberately gitignored. The committed image-recognizer baseline under `src/ask_soony/verifier/baseline_sonnet/` supplies vetted readings for the original document set; readings for new portal documents stay in `data/store/image_recognizer/`.

## Technology

| Layer | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service and CLI | Python 3.13+, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic |
| Data and documents | SQLite, pandas, openpyxl, pypdf/pypdfium2, Pillow, Tesseract in the container |
| Agents | Anthropic, OpenAI, or an OpenAI-compatible local endpoint such as llama.cpp |
| Web app | React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Radix UI, D3/TopoJSON |
| Delivery | Docker multi-stage build: Vite frontend plus Python service |

## Repository map

| Location | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `src/ask_soony/cli.py` | `ask-soony` command-line entry point |
| `src/ask_soony/watcher.py`, `store.py`, `portal.py` | Portal polling, immutable version storage, and portal API access |
| `src/ask_soony/dispatch/`, `verifier/` | Document/ERP linking, contradiction checks, shortfall calculation, and decision payloads |
| `src/ask_soony/predictor/` | LLM-assisted impact analysis for notices, news, logistics, and shipments |
| `src/ask_soony/api.py` | FastAPI application, state composition, approval endpoints, and built-UI serving |
| `src/ask_soony/cardtools.py`, `replies.py`, `outbox.py` | Approved email delivery, supplier-reply matching, and sent-mail reconciliation |
| `src/ask_soony/alerts.py`, `calls.py`, `push.py`, `teams.py` | Optional notification, escalation, call, push, and Teams integrations |
| `src/ask_soony/routines.py` | Approval-aware, sandboxed repeatable actions |
| `web/src/` | Live React decision-inbox UI |
| `web/globe/` | Parked earlier globe prototype; it is not the live UI |
| `tests/`, `src/ask_soony/verifier/**/tests/` | API, workflow, routing, verification, and impact tests |
| `docs/challenge.md`, `plan.md`, `strategy.md` | Challenge context, agreed design, and product rationale |

- Python **3.13 or newer**
- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)

- A Soony portal token to download or continuously poll customer data

```bash
git clone <repository-url>
cd ask-soony
uv sync --group dev

cp .env.example .env
cd web && npm ci && npm run build && cd ..
```

Add only the integrations you intend to use to `.env`; it is gitignored. The portal URL is already present in the template.

| Need | Required settings |
| --- | --- |
| Download/poll the Soony portal | `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN` |
| Anthropic-backed analysis (default) | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| OpenAI-backed analysis | `ASK_LLM_PROVIDER=openai`, plus `ASK_LLM_API_KEY` or an environment-discovered OpenAI key |
| Local OpenAI-compatible model | `ASK_LLM_PROVIDER=llamacpp`, `ASK_LLM_BASE_URL` |
| Run without model calls | `ASK_LLM_PROVIDER=none` |
| Protect the web app | `ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` |
| Send and reconcile supplier mail | `ASK_MAIL_ADDRESS`, `ASK_MAIL_PASSWORD`, `ASK_SMTP_HOST`, and `ASK_IMAP_HOST` |
| Run optional background integrations | `ASK_BACKGROUND=on`; configure the relevant push, Teams, call, or alert settings from `.env.example` |

## Run locally

Build the frontend before using the Python server; FastAPI serves `web/dist` when it exists.

### Decision inbox over existing local state

```bash
uv run ask-soony serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:8000>. This starts the UI and API only; it does not poll the portal. It is useful for inspecting an existing portal mirror and state directory.

### Decision inbox with portal polling and pipeline refresh

```bash
uv run ask-soony run --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
```

This starts the same web service and a background portal loop. Each first poll establishes a baseline; later new or changed paths are recorded as events and routed through verification. Notices, news, logistics, and shipment changes are also eligible for impact prediction when an LLM backend is configured. The polling period defaults to 300 seconds and can be changed with `ASK_INTERVAL_SECONDS` or `--interval`.

For frontend development with Vite hot reload, use:

```bash
scripts/dashboard.sh
```

That starts the API on port 8000 and Vite on <http://localhost:5173>, proxying `/api` to the service.

All commands are available through `uv run ask-soony --help`.

```bash
# Fetch the current portal state into data/portal/ and record it in the version store.
uv run ask-soony download

# Record one portal poll. The first poll is a baseline by default.
uv run ask-soony poll

# Queue stored files under a path and process them with the configured analyst.
uv run ask-soony analyze --path suppliers/<supplier-id>/notices/

# Poll, analyse, notify, and refresh the pipeline in a terminal loop.
uv run ask-soony watch

# Recompute pipeline output from files already in the local mirror.
uv run ask-soony refresh soony/erp/stock_snapshot.csv

# Run or inspect event-impact analysis.
uv run ask-soony predict
uv run ask-soony predict --list

# Rehearse a new portal drop against the local mirror.
uv run ask-soony drop suppliers/<supplier-id>/notices/example.pdf --from ./example.pdf

# Inspect stored versions and open findings.
uv run ask-soony status
uv run ask-soony findings
```

`ask-soony download`, `poll`, `watch`, and `run` need `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN`. `analyze` and LLM-backed `predict` need a configured model provider. `ASK_LLM_PROVIDER=none` leaves portal storage and deterministic verification available while disabling model calls.

## Safety and action model

Lighthouse is designed to act without bypassing people or evidence:

- A decision card retains the contradictory sources and evidence anchors that produced it.
- UI actions are recorded in state first. An approved email is deliverable only to a contact trusted from the supplier master data or an existing matched reply; arbitrary typed recipients are rejected.
- Supplier replies are matched back to prior sent messages by email thread (with a conservative subject fallback), then recorded on the originating decision.
- The shared mailbox's Sent folder can be reconciled so manually sent supplier messages are visible before another draft is sent.
- Repeated work can become a routine, but routines are sandboxed and use a trust ladder. Actions that cost money or change the plan remain approval-gated.
- Call, push, Teams, and email integrations are optional. The default call provider is `dry_run`.

## Tests and checks

```bash
# Python tests, including verifier tests
uv run pytest -q

# Python lint
uv run ruff check .

# Type-check and production-build the web app
cd web && npm run build

# Run the configured web linter
cd web && npm run lint
```

The test suite uses temporary fixtures and is designed not to load a developer's real `.env` file.

## Container deployment

The included `Dockerfile` builds the Vite app and starts the combined service with:

```text
ask-soony run --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT
```

Build and run it locally:

```bash
docker build -t lighthouse .
docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 \
  -e SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN \
  -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY \
  -e ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD \
  lighthouse
```

For a persistent deployment, provide persistent storage for the runtime `data/` directory and configure secrets through the hosting platform rather than baking them into the image. At minimum, a polling deployment needs `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN`; add a model key only for LLM-backed analysis. Set `ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` before exposing the dashboard beyond a trusted network.

## Challenge context

The product problem, constraints, and expected deliverables are in [docs/challenge.md](docs/challenge.md). The team’s current product and module plan is in [plan.md](plan.md); [strategy.md](strategy.md) records the narrower verification-first rationale.

For repository workflow and agent instructions, read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

# Lighthouse

Lighthouse is our entry for the **Lio "Keep the Line Running"** challenge at START Hack Munich 2026. It is an AI-assisted launch-control system for Soony, a fictional games publisher preparing to ship *Grand Heist 6*.

Soony's source of truth is scattered across ERP exports, spreadsheets, PDFs, scans, supplier correspondence, and logistics data. Lighthouse treats every number as a claim: it checks the claim against its evidence, calculates the packing impact, and puts an approval-gated next action in front of the person who can make it happen.

> Customer and portal data are confidential hackathon material. Fetch them only through the portal API, keep them in the gitignored `data/` directory, and do not share or commit them.

## What it does

- Watches the portal for new or changed files, preserving each observed version by checksum.
- Reads changing, imperfect data layouts rather than relying on supplier-specific file names or hard-coded launch quantities.
- Links purchase orders, confirmations, shipping information, goods receipts, stock, and document readings; it preserves disagreements instead of silently choosing a side.
- Calculates usable stock, incoming supply, shortfalls, packing slack, and the time a packing line will run dry.
- Uses an LLM-backed event-impact agent to trace relevant notices, news, logistics, and shipment changes through the supply network.
- Presents evidence-backed decision cards in a React decision inbox, plus launch, supplier, routine, history, warehouse-count, and sign-off views.
- Keeps actions human-approved: an approved supplier email is sent only to a known supplier contact; decisions, replies, sign-offs, and any resulting commitments remain attached to the card.
- Supports optional push notifications, Teams messages, escalation calls, voice-assisted decisions, shared-mailbox reconciliation, and controlled routines.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Portal[Soony portal API] --> Watcher[Portal watcher]
  Watcher --> Store[Version store and portal mirror]
  Store --> Verify[Verifier and shortfall calculation]
  Store --> Predict[Event-impact agent]
  Verify --> State[data/state]
  Predict --> State
  State --> API[FastAPI state API]
  API --> UI[React decision inbox]
  UI --> Approval[Human approval or sign-off]
  Approval --> Action[Known-contact email, warehouse request, or escalation]
  Action --> State
```

The portal watcher stores raw versions in `data/store/` and mirrors current files to `data/portal/`. The dispatch pipeline writes its combined verification payload to `data/state/dispatch.json`; the impact agent writes event analyses to `data/state/event_impacts.json`. The API combines those files with the current portal mirror at request time, so a missing or failed optional module does not take down the inbox.

`data/` is deliberately gitignored. The committed image-recognizer baseline under `src/ask_soony/verifier/baseline_sonnet/` supplies vetted readings for the original document set; readings for new portal documents stay in `data/store/image_recognizer/`.

## Technology

| Layer | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service and CLI | Python 3.13+, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic |
| Data and documents | SQLite, pandas, openpyxl, pypdf/pypdfium2, Pillow, Tesseract in the container |
| Agents | Anthropic, OpenAI, or an OpenAI-compatible local endpoint such as llama.cpp |
| Web app | React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Radix UI, D3/TopoJSON |
| Delivery | Docker multi-stage build: Vite frontend plus Python service |

## Repository map

| Location | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `src/ask_soony/cli.py` | `ask-soony` command-line entry point |
| `src/ask_soony/watcher.py`, `store.py`, `portal.py` | Portal polling, immutable version storage, and portal API access |
| `src/ask_soony/dispatch/`, `verifier/` | Document/ERP linking, contradiction checks, shortfall calculation, and decision payloads |
| `src/ask_soony/predictor/` | LLM-assisted impact analysis for notices, news, logistics, and shipments |
| `src/ask_soony/api.py` | FastAPI application, state composition, approval endpoints, and built-UI serving |
| `src/ask_soony/cardtools.py`, `replies.py`, `outbox.py` | Approved email delivery, supplier-reply matching, and sent-mail reconciliation |
| `src/ask_soony/alerts.py`, `calls.py`, `push.py`, `teams.py` | Optional notification, escalation, call, push, and Teams integrations |
| `src/ask_soony/routines.py` | Approval-aware, sandboxed repeatable actions |
| `web/src/` | Live React decision-inbox UI |
| `web/globe/` | Parked earlier globe prototype; it is not the live UI |
| `tests/`, `src/ask_soony/verifier/**/tests/` | API, workflow, routing, verification, and impact tests |
| `docs/challenge.md`, `plan.md`, `strategy.md` | Challenge context, agreed design, and product rationale |

## Prerequisites

- Python **3.13 or newer**
- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)
- Node.js compatible with the current Vite toolchain (the production Docker build uses Node 22.11)
- A Soony portal token to download or continuously poll customer data

## Setup

```bash
git clone <repository-url>
cd ask-soony
uv sync --group dev

cp .env.example .env
cd web && npm ci && npm run build && cd ..
```

Add only the integrations you intend to use to `.env`; it is gitignored. The portal URL is already present in the template.

| Need | Required settings |
| --- | --- |
| Download/poll the Soony portal | `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN` |
| Anthropic-backed analysis (default) | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| OpenAI-backed analysis | `ASK_LLM_PROVIDER=openai`, plus `ASK_LLM_API_KEY` or an environment-discovered OpenAI key |
| Local OpenAI-compatible model | `ASK_LLM_PROVIDER=llamacpp`, `ASK_LLM_BASE_URL` |
| Run without model calls | `ASK_LLM_PROVIDER=none` |
| Protect the web app | `ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` |
| Send and reconcile supplier mail | `ASK_MAIL_ADDRESS`, `ASK_MAIL_PASSWORD`, `ASK_SMTP_HOST`, and `ASK_IMAP_HOST` |
| Run optional background integrations | `ASK_BACKGROUND=on`; configure the relevant push, Teams, call, or alert settings from `.env.example` |

The OpenAI image recognizer, reply summarizer, and OpenAI realtime calls use `OPENAI_API_KEY` when those features are enabled. See [`.env.example`](.env.example) for the full supported configuration surface.

## Run locally

Build the frontend before using the Python server; FastAPI serves `web/dist` when it exists.

### Decision inbox over existing local state

```bash
uv run ask-soony serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:8000>. This starts the UI and API only; it does not poll the portal. It is useful for inspecting an existing portal mirror and state directory.

### Decision inbox with portal polling and pipeline refresh

```bash
uv run ask-soony run --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
```

This starts the same web service and a background portal loop. Each first poll establishes a baseline; later new or changed paths are recorded as events and routed through verification. Notices, news, logistics, and shipment changes are also eligible for impact prediction when an LLM backend is configured. The polling period defaults to 300 seconds and can be changed with `ASK_INTERVAL_SECONDS` or `--interval`.

For frontend development with Vite hot reload, use:

```bash
scripts/dashboard.sh
```

That starts the API on port 8000 and Vite on <http://localhost:5173>, proxying `/api` to the service.

## Portal and analysis commands

All commands are available through `uv run ask-soony --help`.

```bash
# Fetch the current portal state into data/portal/ and record it in the version store.
uv run ask-soony download

# Record one portal poll. The first poll is a baseline by default.
uv run ask-soony poll

# Queue stored files under a path and process them with the configured analyst.
uv run ask-soony analyze --path suppliers/<supplier-id>/notices/

# Poll, analyse, notify, and refresh the pipeline in a terminal loop.
uv run ask-soony watch

# Recompute pipeline output from files already in the local mirror.
uv run ask-soony refresh soony/erp/stock_snapshot.csv

# Run or inspect event-impact analysis.
uv run ask-soony predict
uv run ask-soony predict --list

# Rehearse a new portal drop against the local mirror.
uv run ask-soony drop suppliers/<supplier-id>/notices/example.pdf --from ./example.pdf

# Inspect stored versions and open findings.
uv run ask-soony status
uv run ask-soony findings
```

`ask-soony download`, `poll`, `watch`, and `run` need `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN`. `analyze` and LLM-backed `predict` need a configured model provider. `ASK_LLM_PROVIDER=none` leaves portal storage and deterministic verification available while disabling model calls.

## Safety and action model

Lighthouse is designed to act without bypassing people or evidence:

- A decision card retains the contradictory sources and evidence anchors that produced it.
- UI actions are recorded in state first. An approved email is deliverable only to a contact trusted from the supplier master data or an existing matched reply; arbitrary typed recipients are rejected.
- Supplier replies are matched back to prior sent messages by email thread (with a conservative subject fallback), then recorded on the originating decision.
- The shared mailbox's Sent folder can be reconciled so manually sent supplier messages are visible before another draft is sent.
- Repeated work can become a routine, but routines are sandboxed and use a trust ladder. Actions that cost money or change the plan remain approval-gated.
- Call, push, Teams, and email integrations are optional. The default call provider is `dry_run`.

## Tests and checks

```bash

uv run pytest -q

# Python lint
uv run ruff check .

# Type-check and production-build the web app
cd web && npm run build

# Run the configured web linter
cd web && npm run lint
```

The test suite uses temporary fixtures and is designed not to load a developer's real `.env` file.

## Container deployment

The included `Dockerfile` builds the Vite app and starts the combined service with:

```text
ask-soony run --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT
```

Build and run it locally:

```bash

  -e SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN \
  -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY \
  -e ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD \

```

For a persistent deployment, provide persistent storage for the runtime `data/` directory and configure secrets through the hosting platform rather than baking them into the image. At minimum, a polling deployment needs `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN`; add a model key only for LLM-backed analysis. Set `ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` before exposing the dashboard beyond a trusted network.

The product problem, constraints, and expected deliverables are in [docs/challenge.md](docs/challenge.md). The team’s current product and module plan is in [plan.md](plan.md); [strategy.md](strategy.md) records the narrower verification-first rationale.

For repository workflow and agent instructions, read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

- **Today** — one evidence-backed decision at a time
- **Launch** — what is at risk, when a line could run dry, and which part is limiting
- **Suppliers** — open cases, shipments, and relationship context
- **Evidence** — the source document and the ERP or planning claim side by side
- **Routines** — repeatable work that can be suggested, reviewed, and gradually trusted

Behind the scenes, Lighthouse watches for new portal files, preserves every file version, verifies the data, calculates shortfalls, and traces relevant world events through the supply network.

## How it works

```text
Portal files → verify claims → calculate launch impact → decision inbox → approved action
```

The system is built to be trustworthy:

- Nothing about a supplier, part, quantity, or deadline is hard-coded.
- New or changed files are detected and processed at runtime.
- Contradictions stay visible, with their source and age.
- Supplier replies are tied back to the original case.
- Money or plan changes remain human-approved.

Customer data stays local in gitignored `data/`. It is confidential hackathon material and must not be committed or shared.

## Run it

### Prerequisites

- Python 3.13+
- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)
- Node.js (the production image uses Node 22)
- A Soony portal token for live data

```bash
git clone <repository-url>
cd ask-soony
uv sync --group dev

cp .env.example .env
cd web && npm ci && npm run build && cd ..
```

Add the secrets and integrations you need to `.env`:

| For | Settings |
| --- | --- |
| Portal download and polling | `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN` |
| Default AI analysis | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| OpenAI analysis | `ASK_LLM_PROVIDER=openai`, `ASK_LLM_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| Local OpenAI-compatible model | `ASK_LLM_PROVIDER=llamacpp`, `ASK_LLM_BASE_URL` |
| No model calls | `ASK_LLM_PROVIDER=none` |
| Password-protected dashboard | `ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` |
| Supplier email and replies | `ASK_MAIL_ADDRESS`, `ASK_MAIL_PASSWORD`, `ASK_SMTP_HOST`, `ASK_IMAP_HOST` |

See [`.env.example`](.env.example) for optional push, Teams, call, voice, and alert settings.

### Start the decision inbox

```bash
# UI and API over local state
uv run ask-soony serve --port 8000

# UI, API, portal polling, and pipeline refresh
uv run ask-soony run --port 8000
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:8000>. The first portal poll establishes a baseline; later changes create events and refresh the relevant checks. Set `ASK_INTERVAL_SECONDS` to change the default five-minute polling interval.

For frontend development:

```bash
scripts/dashboard.sh
```

This starts the API on port 8000 and Vite with hot reload on <http://localhost:5173>.

## Useful commands

```bash
# Fetch the current portal state
uv run ask-soony download

# Poll once, or keep watching and analysing
uv run ask-soony poll
uv run ask-soony watch

# Rebuild decisions from a changed local portal file
uv run ask-soony refresh soony/erp/stock_snapshot.csv

# Inspect findings and event impact
uv run ask-soony findings
uv run ask-soony predict

# Rehearse a new file landing in the portal
uv run ask-soony drop suppliers/<supplier-id>/notices/example.pdf --from ./example.pdf
```

Run `uv run ask-soony --help` for the full command list.

## Built with

- Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn, SQLite, pandas, and document/OCR tooling
- Anthropic, OpenAI, or a local OpenAI-compatible model
- React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and D3
- Docker for deployment

The main application lives in `src/ask_soony/`; the live UI is in `web/src/`. `web/globe/` is an earlier parked prototype, not the live product.

## Quality checks

```bash
uv run pytest -q
uv run ruff check .
cd web && npm run build
cd web && npm run lint
```

## Deploy

The included `Dockerfile` builds the frontend and starts Lighthouse with portal polling:

```bash
docker build -t lighthouse .
docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 \
  -e SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN \
  -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY \
  -e ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD \
  lighthouse
```

Use persistent storage for `data/` in a real deployment, and set `ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` before exposing the dashboard outside a trusted network.

## More context

[docs/challenge.md](docs/challenge.md) contains the challenge brief. [plan.md](plan.md) and [strategy.md](strategy.md) describe the team’s product direction and verification-first approach. For repository workflow, read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

His dream is an ERP that is clean and 100 % trustworthy. 2. He wants less human error. Receipts and other bookings are typed in by hand. Line them up with the ERP and the spreadsheets, and show where they disagree with the evidence for both sides. Never pick a side silently. 2. **Price it:** turn each contradiction into copies at risk. 3. **Act:** send the request to whoever can settle it: supplier, Hamburg, or an approver. 4. **Close the loop:** read the reply and update the claim. ## Scope **We build step 1 first.** It's the hard part: messy files, scans, four languages, and data that changes during the hack. This is also the agent's first real action, which the jury asks for ("do agents act or only summarize?"). Steps 2 to 4 (price, route, close the loop) come after that. ## Pitch line "Soony's numbers are claims. We check them against the paper before the dock does, and once a booking matches the paper, nobody has to type it again." ### questions.md # Questions for Soony Office hours are 10 minutes per person. We need this for the business case. ## Felix Brunner (Senior Buyer) 4. **How often does SAP disagree with what's actually on the pallet, and who notices?** Example: art books are booked as 80,000, but the delivery note says 8,000 (handwritten correction). 5. **Which supplier documents does nobody have time to read?** Karton's downtime notice (in Polish) arrived 9 Nov and is not reflected anywhere. 6. **Which GH6 sleeve artwork is released: rev. B or rev. C?** Karton prints C, PackRight prints B. If only B is valid, the Standard line is about 64,000 sleeves short. ## Nils Berger (IT & Systems) 7. **Can we write back to SAP (block a lot, correct a receipt), or only propose changes?** 8. **Can our agent read and send from the buyers' supplier inbox?** ### inconsistencies_soony.md # Inconsistencies in the Soony data Soony's own data (`soony/`). Nowak rush (4 h load + ~9 h truck) must be ordered **tonight** to arrive in time | | Statue | 13,900 | 8,300 (5,600 failed lot) | 11,700 | **−3,400** without concession | | Sleeve | 116,000 | ≥48,000 even without rev B and the GH5 pallet | 38,000 | ok, pull the wrong pallet | | Steel case / box / poster | 17,900 / 14,000 / 26,500 | same | 11,700 | ok | The stock update writes quantities as text with dots as thousands separators (`'42.900'`): parsers must handle it. Demo path: **#1 end to end first.** It now has a real deadline: the criticality agent must work out that the Nowak order has to go out tonight. Then #3 (early catch) and #8 (cases), then the rest. ## 4. Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR P[Portal API] --> W[Watcher
Jonas] W --> V[Verification
Farhan] W --> F[Arrival forecast
Lucas] V --> C[Criticality agent
Jonas] F --> C C --> A[Actions: call, email, notify
Jonas] A --> T[Trust gate
allow once / always] V --> UI[Platform UI
Akshat] F --> UI C --> UI T --> UI ``` Every module reads and writes the shared shapes below, stored as JSON files under `data/state/` (gitignored). Modules never call each other directly; the UI reads the same state. ### Shared shapes (agree before coding, live in `src/ask_soony/schema.py`) ```text Claim { id, kind: quantity|date|status|revision|terms|iban|eta, part, po, po_line, shipment, supplier, value, unit, source_doc, page, quote, language, confidence, seen_at } Finding { id, kind: mismatch|stale|risk_news|forecast_late, claims: [claim ids], sides: [{source, value}], summary, part, created_at, status: open|resolved|dismissed } Impact { finding_id, part, units_short, copies_at_risk, edition, cell_hours_lost, deadline, slack_hours } Decision { finding_id, severity: call|email|notify|log, reason, approver, options: [{action, cost, effect}] } Action { id, decision_id, channel: call|email|portal, to, draft, trust: ask|allow_once|allow_always, status: draft|approved|sent|replied, reply } ``` ## 5. Who does what ### Jonas: watcher, criticality agent, calls and emails - **Watcher (in progress):** poll the portal, keep every file version, emit a change event per new or changed file. - **Criticality agent:** for each Finding + Impact, decide `call | email | notify | log`: - Code computes the hard numbers: copies at risk, Collector's cell hours lost (900/h), slack left before Sun 20:00 (all read from the plan and master data). - Agent judges what the code can't: is this a real risk or a false alarm (magnets), and who approves the fix. Reads the org chart and approval policy PP-07; if the approver post is vacant, finds the deputy or next level. - Output: a Decision with options, each with a cost and an effect ("accept Nowak rush offer: 8,000 books, Annex A price, truck arrives ~13 h after order"). ### strategy.md # Strategy ## The problem Soony's systems drift away from the paper trail, and nobody notices until the dock. Almost every launch-critical finding follows the same pattern: the number in SAP or a spreadsheet is wrong, and a document already said so. - Art books: SAP says 80,000, the delivery note says 8,000 (handwritten). - Statues: stock says usable, the inspection report says the lot failed. - Game cards: the shipment feed says 48,000, the shipping advice says 28,000. - Karton: no capacity limit anywhere, but a Polish notice from 9 Nov says the plant is down all weekend. The truth was in an unread scan, a foreign-language PDF or a confirmation remark. The opposite also happens: magnets look 100,800 short, but the contract annex says they come fitted in the box. This happens at every company with an ERP and outside suppliers, on every order. A launch only makes the cost visible. ## What Soony told us Nils Berger (IT & Systems Lead), Saturday: 1. His dream is an ERP that is clean and 100 % trustworthy. 2. He wants less human error. Receipts and other bookings are typed in by hand. Our answer is one engine pointed two ways: - **Detect:** find what is already wrong in SAP (step 1, the verifier). - **Prevent:** read the delivery note and fill in the booking, so a person only confirms. The S1 error (80,000 typed where the note says 8,000) can't happen. Prevention comes almost free once step 1 works, because the verifier already pulls out every field a receipt needs. ## The product Every number in the plan is a claim. We check each claim against the documents that confirm or contradict it. 1. **Verify:** read every document and pull out claims (quantity, date, status, revision, price). Line them up with the ERP and the spreadsheets, and show where they disagree with the evidence for both sides. Never pick a side silently. 2. **Price it:** turn each contradiction into copies at risk. 3. **Act:** send the request to whoever can settle it: supplier, Hamburg, or an approver. 4. **Close the loop:** read the reply and update the claim. ## Scope **We build step 1 first.** It's the hard part: messy files, scans, four languages, and data that changes during the hack. Start narrow, with three claim types where the evidence is clear: - **Quantity received:** delivery note vs. goods receipt (S1) - **Quantity and date shipped:** shipping advice or confirmation vs. shipment feed (P2, P13) - **Quality status:** inspection report vs. stock status (S2) Add more types only once these three work on new files without code changes. **Then: prevent.** Prefilled goods receipts from delivery-note scans, confirmed by a person. This is also the agent's first real action, which the jury asks for ("do agents act or only summarize?"). Steps 2 to 4 (price, route, close the loop) come after that. ## Pitch line "Soony's numbers are claims. We check them against the paper before the dock does, and once a booking matches the paper, nobody has to type it again." ### questions.md # Questions for Soony Office hours are 10 minutes per person. Only questions the data can't answer and whose answer changes what we build. Most important first. ## Maren Vogt (Head of Procurement) 1. **What does a missing copy cost, Standard vs. Collector's?** Game cards are about 6,800 short across both editions. The answer decides which edition gets them and whether extra air freight is worth paying for. 2. **Who decides for Collector's Items while the Category Lead role is vacant?** That role approves the failed statue lot (5,600 statues), Collector's air freight and the Pune release extension. 3. **What is the annual spend with these six suppliers, and has Soony ever claimed back a price increase?** Four suppliers bill 3 to 7 % above contract. We need this for the business case. ## Felix Brunner (Senior Buyer) 4. **How often does SAP disagree with what's actually on the pallet, and who notices?** Example: art books are booked as 80,000, but the delivery note says 8,000 (handwritten correction). 5. **Which supplier documents does nobody have time to read?** Karton's downtime notice (in Polish) arrived 9 Nov and is not reflected anywhere. 6. **Which GH6 sleeve artwork is released: rev. B or rev. C?** Karton prints C, PackRight prints B. If only B is valid, the Standard line is about 64,000 sleeves short. ## Nils Berger (IT & Systems) 7. **Can we write back to SAP (block a lot, correct a receipt), or only propose changes?** 8. **Can our agent read and send from the buyers' supplier inbox?** ### inconsistencies_soony.md # Inconsistencies in the Soony data Soony's own data (`soony/`). Supplier data: `inconsistencies_suppliers.md` (P…). Each row compares what the system says with what the evidence says. ## Launch-critical | # | System says | Evidence says | Impact | |---|---|---|---| | S1 | Art books: SAP stock 80,000 (batch 5000413065, "over delivery accepted") | Delivery note `receiving/DC-HAM/20261118_WZ-261116-473.jpg`: 80,000 crossed out, 8,000 handwritten. PO 4500318768/3 is for 8,000. | **About 5,900 short** (plan says "ok"). Fix: Karton has 8,000 in stock (P6). | | S2 | Statue lot 5000413063 (5,600) is "unrestricted" | `inspection_report_5000413063.pdf`: 9 of 125 defective, limit 3 | **About 3,400 short** (plan says "ok"). A concession needs the vacant Category Lead (S15). | | S4 | Launch plan counts 48,000 game cards by air, arriving Sat 21 Nov (SHP-2026-04311) | Shipping advice: 28,000 flew; 20,000 arrive Tue 24 Nov (P2). The standard route (S5) also points to Mon 23 Nov. | **About 6,800 short.** 34,800 short if the 28,000 miss Sun 20:00. | | S3 | BOM: 4 magnets per Collector's Edition, stock 0. The plan shows "CHECK" for 100,800. | PackRight contract Annex A: magnets come fitted in the box (P1) | **False alarm.** | ## Other contradictions | # | System says | Evidence says | Impact | |---|---|---|---| | S6 | Excel tracker: 14 shipments | Shipment feed: 25 | The tracker misses both game card air shipments. | | S7 | Tracker: SHP-2026-04276 "in transit" | Feed: arrived at port, available for pick-up | 350,000 game card cases waiting at the Hamburg terminal | | S9 | Plan dated Fri 20 Nov 18:00 | Packing log ends Thu 19 Nov | Friday's output is missing. *To verify.* | | S13 | 78,000 "Pre-order Pin GH6" booked as misc merchandise | No PO, not in master data, not in the BOM | Unordered goods from Dongguan (P20) | ## Gaps that limit checking - **S8** The shipment feed has no quantities, only PO numbers. Quantities have to be inferred from the POs. - **S10** Stock is "not counted": physical counts are 4 to 19 days old. - **S14** Only 69 of 392 receipts have a scanned delivery note, all from Sep 2026 onward. - **S11** GH5 uses the same case and leaflet as GH6, but the plan counts GH6 only. Low risk (large surplus). - **S12** Criticality flags are unreliable: the statue, steel case and Collector's box are not marked critical. ## Ownership gaps - **S15** The Category Lead for Collector's Items is vacant. Concessions, Collector's air freight and supplier releases escalate to the Head of Procurement (PP-07 §6). - **S16** Two Pune statue orders are stuck in "awaiting approval" because the conditional release expired (P17). ## Format quirks (handle in code) - Two PO exports with different layouts. The legacy one uses `;`, decimal commas, `MM/DD/YYYY` dates, numeric supplier ids (`19` = `SUP-0019`) and no currency column. - Cancellations are negative quantities. - Routes go via SGSIN, which is missing from `master/ports.csv`. - The tracker uses supplier names; the ERP uses supplier ids. ## Next - Check the other 57 delivery-note scans for handwritten corrections like S1. This is the verifier's first job. ### inconsistencies_suppliers.md # Inconsistencies in the supplier data Supplier data (`suppliers/`). Soony data: `inconsistencies_soony.md` (S…). All 229 supplier PDFs were read, and every confirmation was checked line by line against SAP. ## Launch-critical | # | System says | Evidence says | Impact | |---|---|---|---| | P2 | Feed and plan: 48,000 Hwaseong game cards arrive 21 Nov (SHP-2026-04311) | `Shipping_advice_020-48113256_4500318735.pdf` (appeared 21 Nov): 28,000 flew, 20,000 arrive Tue 24 Nov | **About 6,800 game cards short** (S4). Late delivery qualifies for LTA §7 damages of about $3.9k/week. | | P3 | Master data: GH6 sleeve rev. B | Karton confirmations print rev. C ("received from Soony Marketing 2026-08-07"); PackRight prints rev. B | Hamburg holds 122,000 rev. C and 64,000 rev. B sleeves. **If only rev. B is valid: about 64,000 short.** | | P4 | Nothing (no capacity limit anywhere) | Polish notice dated 9 Nov: Karton's offset printing and bindery are down Sat 14:00 to Mon 06:00 | No reprints before launch. Karton's rush offer (P5) contradicts this notice, and rush printing lands too late anyway. | | P6 | Nothing | Karton offer of 21 Nov: 8,000 art books from stock, loaded in 4 h, plus about 9 h by truck | **Fixes S1.** €16,800, so a buyer can approve it. Expires 22 Nov. Needs a dock slot. | | P16 | Profile: Pune `conditional`, release expired 30 Oct | All Pune confirmations claim "approved for serial supply" | Explains why the failed lot was booked as usable (S2) | | P13 | Feed: Boise SHP-2026-04314 "booked" for 21 Nov. SAP: DDP Hamburg | Confirmation for PO 4500318769: on hold until Soony confirms EXW in writing. The contract says EXW. | 36,000 cards stuck. After launch anyway. Fix: one email. | | P1 | BOM: magnets are a separate part, stock 0 | PackRight contract Annex A: fitted in the Collector's box | **False alarm** (S3) | ## Confirmations vs. SAP (not launch-critical) - **P12, P15, P7** Order lines with no supplier confirmation: Hwaseong 5, Boise 7, Karton 2 POs, PackRight 3. Boise's unconfirmed line is on a plane (SHP-2026-04310). Karton's unconfirmed PO has a truck booked (SHP-2026-04316). - **P10** Hwaseong PO 4500318636: SAP promises 26 May, the confirmation says 9 Jun. ## Prices vs. contract (business case, not launch) | # | Supplier | Contract says | Billed | |---|---|---|---| | P9 | Hwaseong | GH5 card fixed at $5.40 until expiry | Confirmations quote $5.51 to $5.62 (SAP keeps $5.40) | | P14 | Boise | 60 days' notice for price changes | +4 % and +3 % effective immediately, accepted in SAP | | P18 | Dongguan | No price-revision clause | +3 % twice in 2026, 30 lines overpaid | | P22 | PackRight | Prices fixed for the calendar year | +4 % mid-2025 | - **P8** Supplier `components.csv` files still carry the old prices, so cost calculations from them come out 3 to 7 % too low. ## Structural risks (after launch) - **P11** Hwaseong (game cards, 70 % share): contract expires 31 Dec. Renewal must be signed by **15 Dec**. Open PO 4500318783 (134,000 cards) is unconfirmed. - **P19** Dongguan (steel case, sole source): contract ends 28 Feb 2027. The Chinese New Year shutdown schedule is due 30 Nov. - **P21** PackRight's box magnets come from a rare-earth sub-supplier (Jiangxi RareMag). Export restrictions count as force majeure, which makes it a single point of failure for every future Collector's Edition. - **P17** Pune orders placed after 30 Oct are blocked, as the policy says. Only the vacant Category Lead can extend the release. ## Other - **P20** Dongguan shipped 78,000 pre-order pins without a PO (same as S13). - **P23** PackRight uses its own part numbers. Contract Annex C maps them to Soony's. ## Contract facts | Supplier | Parts (share) | Incoterm | Expires | Clause to know | |---|---|---|---|---| | SUP-0010 Hwaseong (KR) | game cards (70 %) | FOB Busan | 31 Dec 2026 | §7 late delivery: 2 %/week, max 10 % | | SUP-0011 Boise (US) | game cards (30 %) | EXW Boise | | Delay liability capped at price | | SUP-0018 Pune (IN) | statue (20 %) | | | §2.2 conditional release only | | SUP-0019 Dongguan (CN) | steel case (100 %), statue (80 %), clear case (40 %) | FOB Yantian | 28 Feb 2027 | No price revisions allowed | | SUP-0028 Karton (PL) | sleeve, art book, poster, leaflet | DAP Hamburg | 31 Dec 2027 | §3.2 rush orders; §6.2 prints the artwork Soony last released in writing | | SUP-0029 PackRight (CN) | Collector's box (100 %), clear case (60 %), sleeve (40 %) | FOB Yantian | 31 Aug 2027 | §8 force majeure covers rare-earth export restrictions | --- local runtime assets --- --- available browser tooling --- /opt/homebrew/bin/npx --- built UI ---
